ideaData.title: Swappable-insert megacast die builds both MHEV and BEV rear floors
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: a luxury SUV platform that casts its rear floor usually needs two different rear underbody castings – the MHEV version with exhaust-silencer pocket, fuel-tank saddle and spare-wheel well, and the BEV version with rear-EDU cradle bosses and a pack rear flange – meaning two 6,000-9,000 t class die sets (≈€3.5-4.5M each) or a fallback to a ~70-part stamped rear floor for one powertrain. Proposal: one rear megacast die (AlSi10MnMg, vacuum HPDC) whose variant geometry is concentrated in three replaceable core inserts of ≤350 kg each – silencer/spare-well pocket vs rear-EDU cradle bosses, tank saddle vs pack flange, filler vs charge-port pocket – exchanged on a quick-die-change rack in <45 min inside the planned die-spray/maintenance window. Rear rail sections, damper-mount and towbar-node geometry and all body-side datums stay identical, so one framing fixture, one measurement program and one trim die serve both powertrains. At 50,000/yr (e.g. 60/40 MHEV/BEV) the cell runs two-shift campaigns per variant. Why it works: the variant content of a rear floor is local (pockets, bosses), not global (rails, load paths), so it fits in inserts; insert parting lines are placed on non-cosmetic, low-stress flanges. Benchmark: Volvo chose the rear floor for its EX60 megacasting because that zone carries the seating, suspension and powertrain-configuration parts, replacing 60-100 welded steel components with one HPDC part 15-20% lighter than steel.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: The second megacast die set, its trim die and CNC fixtures are never bought; die spares and maintenance are pooled on one tool; both powertrains share one casting cell, so the press is loaded at 50,000/yr instead of two under-loaded variants.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: One casting cell, one trim press and one machining fixture family; insert change adds ~45 min per campaign (≈2 changes/week). Insert rack and handling crane ≈€0.2M. Scrap risk at insert parting lines handled by vacuum level <50 mbar and local squeeze pins.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Body-side datums (3-2-1 RPS) identical for both variants, so framing and measurement fixtures are common; variant poka-yoke by cast-in insert ID letter read by the in-cell camera before trim, preventing a BEV casting entering an MHEV body.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Medium – large tooling avoidance amortised over a modest 50,000/yr volume
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Second die set avoided €3.5-4.5M ÷ 350,000 = €10.0-€12.9; duplicate trim die + CNC fixtures avoided €0.9M ÷ 350,000 = €2.6; pooled die spares €0.6-€1.0; minus insert-change downtime and insert wear €2.2 (low) / €1.6 (high). Low = 10.0+2.6+0.6-2.2 = €11.0; high = 12.9+2.6+1.0-1.6 = €14.9. Net €11-€14.9 per vehicle × 50,000 vehicles/yr = €0.55M-€0.745M per year (estimate; amortisation over 7 years = 350,000 vehicles where stated).

ideaData.riskNotes: Insert flash and heat-checking at parting lines; dimensional drift between variants. Validate by CT/X-ray to ASTM E505 level 2 on 3 lots per variant, rear impact (UN R34/FMVSS 301 fuel-system and ECE R100 pack integrity for BEV) and 3,500 kg towing fatigue. Mitigate with insert seating datums and per-variant die temperature recipe.

title: Multi-ring-electrode aluminium spot welding replaces self-piercing rivets on closures
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Removes ~300 rivet consumables per vehicle and the SPR punch/die wear; welding guns reach joint configurations rivet guns cannot, reducing dedicated tooling; electricity and cap dressing cost far less than rivets. Benchmark: GM's patented multi-ring domed electrode welds sheet, extruded and cast aluminium, was used on the Cadillac CTS-V hood and the Tahoe/Yukon hybrid liftgate, and was expected to eliminate nearly two pounds of rivets from hoods, liftgates and doors while avoiding retooling cost.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Removes ~300 rivet consumables per vehicle and the SPR punch/die wear; welding guns reach joint configurations rivet guns cannot, reducing dedicated tooling; electricity and cap dressing cost far less than rivets.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Closure lines replace ~10 SPR guns with servo RSW guns (similar capex, can reuse steel-line robots); weld time ≈0.3-0.5 s vs ~1.5-2 s rivet set; tip dresser per gun. No paint-shop change. Weld lobe set-up per stack.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Single-sided feed systems disappear; flange width stays ≥16 mm; weld-spot pitch 25-35 mm; cap-condition monitoring by adaptive control. Serviceability: welded flanges repaired by bonded rivet per OEM repair manual.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Medium – rivet consumables are the dominant variable cost of Al closure joining
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Rivets deleted 280-340 × €0.025-€0.04 = €7.0-€13.6; SPR die/punch wear and feeder service €1.0-€1.4; minus caps/dressing €2.4 (low) / €1.8 (high) and extra energy €0.3. Low = 7.0+1.0-2.4-0.3 = €5.3; high = 13.6+1.4-1.8-0.3 = €12.9. Net €5.3-€12.9 per vehicle × 50,000 vehicles/yr = €0.265M-€0.645M per year (estimate; amortisation over 7 years = 350,000 vehicles where stated).

ideaData.riskNotes: Al RSW porosity and liquid-metal cracking, electrode life, lower fatigue than SPR in peel. Validate with ISO 14273 shear/ISO 14272 cross-tension coupons, door slam test (≥100k cycles), tailgate slam, salt-spray VDA 233-102 and closure sag/set. Mitigate with adhesive weld-bonding at peel-loaded joints.

title: Wade-line sealing plane: robotic butyl patches below 950 mm, open drains above
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Fewer, cheaper closures (patch vs moulded plug), plug labour eliminated, plug part-number count from ~12 to 2, and lower water-ingress warranty because a robot-placed fused patch cannot be mis-seated. Baseline: a luxury SUV specified for 900 mm wading typically closes every E-coat drain and access hole the same way, regardless of height – 60-90 moulded EPDM/PE push-in plugs in ~12 different sizes, pushed in by hand at trim (≈6 s each), with manual seam-sealer touch-ups – because nobody owns a defined 'wet line'. Proposal: define a body sealing plane at Z = 950 mm above ground at maximum ride height in wade mode (900 mm wade + 50 mm bow-wave margin). Below it: standardise drain holes to three diameters (Ø20/25/30 mm) and close them with heat-activated butyl/PET patches (two sizes) applied by one vision-guided robot after E-coat and before the sealer oven, so the patch fuses in the existing bake (≈160-180 °C); target 35-45 closures. Above it: drains stay open or receive a single PE flap type; sealer there becomes cosmetic only. Why it works: hydrostatic head at the floor in a 900 mm wade is only ≈9 kPa – a bonded patch has margin; a push-in plug's failure mode is mis-seating by hand, which the robot removes. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460 is rated for 900 mm wading, with a Wade Mode that raises ride height, locks the driveline and closes cabin vents.

ideaData.title: Hand-of-drive-neutral body: superset dash piercing and bolt-on pedal and column mounts
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: a luxury SUV sold in LHD and RHD markets usually carries hand-specific BIW content: two dash-panel (bulkhead) variants or a variant pierce station for the steering-column aperture and pedal-box/brake-booster stud pattern, welded hand-specific brackets for the column support, wiper linkage and HVAC drain, and separate framing and sealer programs – multiplied by MHEV/BEV, giving four bulkhead combinations, each with its own part number, sequencing and buffer. Proposal: one dash panel pressing pierced with both column apertures and both pedal-box stud patterns (superset piercing in the low-stress flat zone, ≥25 mm from beads); the unused aperture is closed by a bolt-on PA6-GF30 cover plate with butyl seal and a 2 kg/m² mass layer that restores transmission loss, and every hand-specific bracket moves from the dash (welded) to the magnesium/steel cross-car beam (bolted at trim). The BIW then has one bulkhead for all four variants; hand-of-drive is decided at trim, not in the body shop. Why it works: bulkhead stiffness around the column is set by the cross-car beam and the cowl, not by the small aperture, and covering a pierced hole with a sealed mass-loaded plate keeps the NVH barrier intact. title: Bolt-in tunnel cassette lets MHEV and BEV share one flat front-floor pressing
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] One floor die set and one framing fixture instead of two; the MHEV-specific content becomes a small sub-assembly bought or built at lower cost; BEV avoids carrying tunnel reinforcements it does not need. Proposal: one flat front-floor pressing for both (EN AW-5182-O 2.0 mm in an aluminium body; HX340LAD+Z 0.9 mm in a steel body) with a trimmed central window 260 × 1,250 mm. Why it works: the bonded 30 mm flange in shear (~25 MPa adhesive) restores torsional continuity – the tunnel contributes stiffness only through its perimeter. title: One ultra-high-strength beam per door deletes second beam and belt reinforcement
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Deletes one beam (material, forming, joining) and the belt-line reinforcement per door; the grade upgrade costs far less than the deleted part; lighter doors reduce hinge and check-strap loads. Baseline: luxury SUV front doors (and often rears) carry two side-intrusion members – e.g. an upper 22MnB5 tube Ø32 × 2.0 mm plus a lower stamped hat beam, or one beam plus a stamped belt-line reinforcement – totalling 4.5-6.0 kg of steel per door with 3-5 joining operations. Proposal: a single press-hardened beam in a 2,000 MPa-class grade (e.g. 34MnB5 AS150 / PHS2000-class, 1.6 mm, open hat 60 mm deep with a closing flange) at the pole/MDB impact height, its ends bonded and bolted into the hinge-face and lock-face reinforcements; belt-line bending stiffness for glass support comes from the existing roll-formed DP980 waist rail. The second beam and the belt reinforcement are deleted. Why it works: beam bending capacity scales with yield strength × section modulus – raising Rm from ~1,500 to ~2,000 MPa gives ≈30% more capacity in the same section, enough to carry what two lower-grade members shared; door mass falls ≈1.5 kg per door. Benchmark: Xiaomi YU7 (2025) uses its 2,200 MPa ultra-high-strength steel for the anti-collision beams of all four doors.

title: Cast-to-net datums and cored holes halve rear megacast CNC machining
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Machining time per casting falls by more than half, tapping is eliminated, and fewer 5-axis machining centres are bought for 50,000/yr; die-feature cost is small by comparison. Baseline: a 55-70 kg rear underbody megacast typically passes through a 5-axis machining cell for 25-40 features – damper top-mount faces, sub-frame bores, towbar and seat-anchor faces, datum pins and tapped holes – at ~160-200 s per part, then deburr and wash. Proposal: hold ±0.15 mm on the 12 non-critical bolt faces directly from the die (vacuum HPDC <50 mbar, local squeeze pins under thick bosses, die-temperature control ±10 K) and form 15-18 threaded holes as cast cored holes (0.5° draft) used with thread-forming screws (flow-form into AlSi10MnMg, no tapping). Machining is kept only for the 3-2-1 primary datums, the two sub-frame bores and the damper-mount faces (6-8 features), ~70-80 s per part. Remaining dimensional correction is done in the framing station with an adaptive (shimmed) locator. Why it works: modern vacuum HPDC repeats to ~±0.2 mm on bosses near the gate; only features on the crash/suspension load path need machining accuracy. ideaData.title: Cast-to-net datums and cored holes halve rear megacast CNC machining
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: a 55-70 kg rear underbody megacast typically passes through a 5-axis machining cell for 25-40 features – damper top-mount faces, sub-frame bores, towbar and seat-anchor faces, datum pins and tapped holes – at ~160-200 s per part, then deburr and wash. Proposal: hold ±0.15 mm on the 12 non-critical bolt faces directly from the die (vacuum HPDC <50 mbar, local squeeze pins under thick bosses, die-temperature control ±10 K) and form 15-18 threaded holes as cast cored holes (0.5° draft) used with thread-forming screws (flow-form into AlSi10MnMg, no tapping). Machining is kept only for the 3-2-1 primary datums, the two sub-frame bores and the damper-mount faces (6-8 features), ~70-80 s per part. Remaining dimensional correction is done in the framing station with an adaptive (shimmed) locator. Why it works: modern vacuum HPDC repeats to ~±0.2 mm on bosses near the gate; only features on the crash/suspension load path need machining accuracy. Benchmark: the 2025 Tesla Model Y redesigned its rear casting to shed 7 kg and halve machining time, with processing time per part falling from 180 s to 75 s.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Machining centres for the casting line drop from ~3 to ~1.5 (≈€1.35M avoided); cycle 180 s → 75-80 s; deburr/wash load halved. Die gets squeeze pins and core pins (~€0.4M).

title: 3,500 kg towbar bolts into cast subframe-mount node, deleting rail tow-plates
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes four rail reinforcement plates and their joining on every body, and shortens the tow cross-member by ~4-6 kg on tow-equipped vehicles; adds only cast-in inserts. Baseline: a luxury SUV rated for 3,500 kg towing typically uses a bolted steel tow cross-member (S420MC tube, 9-12 kg) fixed to the rear rail ends with 6-8 M12 bolts, plus four 2.5-3.0 mm reinforcement plates welded or riveted inside the rear rails on every body (tow-prep) to spread the load. Design load: UN R55 D-value = g·T·C/(T+C) = 9.81 × 3,300 × 3,500 / 6,800 ≈ 16.7 kN, with static vertical towball load up to ~150 kg. Proposal: route the towbar into the cast aluminium rear sub-frame-mount node: four M14 steel threaded inserts cast into vacuum-HPDC bosses (or through-bolted), sized for 2 × 10^6 cycles at ±D and a 1.5 × D proof load; the tow cross-member shortens to a 4-5 kg S420MC receiver bracket with detachable ball neck, and the in-rail plates are deleted. Identical for MHEV and BEV. Why it works: the node already carries rear sub-frame loads of similar magnitude, so the boss stress increment is small; the load path is shorter than through thin rail flanges. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460's MLA-Flex uses cast aluminium sections including a one-piece rear-subframe mounting.

title: Contour-following water galleries in press-hardening tools shorten martensite quench dwell
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Shorter press-hardening cycle reduces line-hours per vehicle across all hot-stamped parts, and more uniform quench cuts soft-spot scrap; only the hot-spot inserts are replaced, not whole dies. Baseline: a luxury SUV body carries ~12-14 press-hardened 22MnB5 AS150 parts (door rings, tunnel, cross-members, bumper beams). Their dies use gun-drilled straight cooling channels, which leave hot spots at deep radii (B-pillar head, sill corners) and force a long in-die quench dwell (≈6-10 s) to bring every zone below ~200 °C at ≥27 K/s critical cooling; stroke-to-stroke ~18-22 s, and soft spots drive hardness-scrap. Proposal: re-make only the slow-quenching sections of each press-hardening tool as laser-powder-bed-fused hot-work steel segments with water galleries (Ø6-8 mm) running 8-10 mm under the forming face and following its 3D contour, fed from the existing chilled-water supply. Target: −1.2 to −1.8 s closed-tool dwell per stroke and a uniform martensitic structure (≥470 HV) with no bainitic soft spots. Why it works: the blank's quench rate depends on the steel thickness between water and blank; galleries that follow the radius keep that thickness constant where straight gun-drilling cannot, so the last zone to cool reaches Mf as fast as the rest. Benchmark: US patents 10,610,917 and 11,673,177 describe 3D-printed conformal cooling in cast hot-stamping die insert

title: Third-row seat anchors and damper mounts cast into rear megacast, deleting brackets
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] 14-20 brackets, ~30 weld nuts and their framing/joining operations disappear; casting conversion of a kilogram of features costs far less than separate stampings plus joining. Baseline: a seven-seat luxury SUV rear floor carries third-row seat anchors and latch strikers, ISOFIX bars, cargo tie-down rings, rear damper top-mount reinforcements and seat-belt retractor brackets as 14-20 separate stamped HSLA brackets (1.2-2.0 mm) with ~24-30 weld nuts, all positioned in a framing fixture. Proposal: with a rear megacast in place, cast these as features: seat and belt anchors as bosses with cored holes for M10/M12 thread-forming bolts, damper top-mount as a ribbed dome, ISOFIX as a cast-in 6 mm steel bar insert or a bolted bar on cast bosses, tie-downs as cast eyes. Added casting mass ~0.8-1.2 kg against ~3-4 kg of deleted steel. Why it works: cast bosses in AlSi10MnMg (Rp0.2 ≈ 120-160 MPa, A ≥ 7%) sized with 2.5× wall thickness meet anchor loads, and the casting already spans these locations so no new load path is created. Benchmark: Volvo selected the rear floor for megacasting because that zone holds many parts related to seating, suspension and powertrain configurations; the EX60 casting replaces 60-100 welded steel parts.

title: Rear-rail extrusion-to-node joints welded with oxide-breaking domed caps instead of FDS
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] FDS and SPR consumables on extrusion-to-casting joints disappear, and a spot weld is ~4× faster than a flow-drill screw, freeing robot time in the rear-structure cell. Baseline: in an aluminium-intensive rear structure, 6082-T6 / 6063-T6 extruded longitudinals and cross-members meet the cast rear node at 40-60 joint positions, mostly made with flow-drill screws (≈€0.12-0.14 each, ~2.5 s cycle, single-sided) plus some punched mechanical joints (≈€0.035 each), because resistance welding of die-cast flanges was considered unreliable. Proposal: redesign the node flanges for two-sided gun access and fuse extrusion wall (2.5-3.0 mm) to cast flange (3.0 mm) with ridged-dome caps, MFDC 1 kHz, ≈6-7 kN, 30-40 kA; the node must be vacuum-cast with low dissolved gas (target ≤5 ml/100 g) and ≥7% elongation so the nugget does not open shrinkage pores. FDS stay only where the node geometry blocks the second electrode. Why it works: the ridges break the oxide on both the extruded and the cast surface, so contact resistance is stable and the nugget repeatable; nuggets take shear while the retained epoxy takes peel and seals the crevice. Benchmark: GM's multi-ring domed electrode process welds sheet, extruded and cast aluminium and was used to remove rivets from hoods, liftgates and doors.

title: Body pressure-relief vents moved above wade line with passive check flaps
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes wading baffles/shrouds and the low apertures' sealing, and cuts load-space water-ingress warranty after wading; the longer duct adds less than it removes. Baseline: body pressure-relief (cabin air-extraction) vents usually sit low in the rear quarter behind the bumper fascia, ~350-500 mm above ground – well below a 900 mm wade line – so off-road SUVs add foam wading baffles, labyrinth shrouds or extra seals around the vent apertures, and still see load-space water ingress warranty after deep wading. Proposal: relocate the two vents to the D-pillar upper cavity (Z ≥ 1,100 mm), exhausting into the tailgate gutter/under the roof spoiler through a moulded PP-T20 frame with two EPDM check flaps; delete the low quarter-panel apertures in the body-side inner (no flanged hole, no sealer, no baffle). Required free area (~60-80 cm² per side for door-closing pressure relief) is kept by a taller, narrower duct within the D-pillar trim. Why it works: placing the opening above the wading line removes the hydrostatic path instead of resisting it; a check flap only has to stop spray, not a head of water. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460 is rated for 900 mm wading, with Wade Mode raising ride height, locking the driveline and closing cabin vents.

title: Tailgate aperture lower flange and striker boss cast into rear megacast
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Five to seven stampings and their joining go away; tailgate fitting time and gap/flush rework fall because the striker and lower aperture are fixed by the casting. Baseline: the lower half of a luxury SUV tailgate aperture – rear end panel, D-ring lower corners, tail-lamp pockets and striker reinforcement – is typically 5-7 stampings joined in the rear-end framing, giving a tolerance stack of ~±1.0-1.2 mm at the aperture; final assembly then spends ~60-90 s per car shimming hinges and adjusting the striker to meet gap/flush (e.g. 4.5 ± 0.5 mm) and seal compression, with rework on a share of cars. Proposal: with a rear megacast already in the body, extend it to include the lower aperture flange, lamp pockets and a fixed striker boss (M8 cored holes, no slotted adjustment); the aperture lower edge and striker are then located by the die (±0.3-0.5 mm). Hinges at the roof header remain adjustable, giving one-direction set-up. Why it works: removing 5-7 parts from the stack collapses the tolerance chain to one casting plus one roof-header interface, so the seal compression range narrows and the tailgate closes with consistent effort. Benchmark: the refreshed 2025 Tesla Model Y's new body castings further reduced panel gaps to cut outside noise.

title: Torsional-stiffness target audit deletes surplus roof and D-ring gussets

title: Coil grade-and-gauge catalogue cut from ~30 to 15 across BIW stampings
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Lower mill extras and small-lot premiums on ~€700 of sheet per vehicle, fewer coils in stock, fewer blanking changeovers and better nesting; partly offset by rounding gauges up. Baseline: a mixed steel/aluminium luxury SUV body commonly uses 25-35 distinct coil specifications (grade × gauge × coating × width), e.g. HX180BD, HX220BD, HX260LAD, HX300LAD, HX340LAD, HX380LAD, HX420LAD in 0.05 mm gauge steps, plus 5182-O, 5754-O, 6016-T4, 6014-T4 variants – each bringing mill size/grade extras, minimum order quantities, separate coil storage and blanking changeovers. Proposal: a rationalised catalogue of ≤15 specifications: steel outers on one bake-hardening grade (CR210BH/HX220BD) in two gauges; structural cold-formed grades collapsed to HX340LAD+ZF and CR700Y980T-DP; one press-hardening grade (22MnB5 AS150); aluminium inner/outer on 6016-T4 (inners) and 5182-O only where draw depth demands; gauge steps 0.1 mm instead of 0.05 mm, rounding up (mass penalty ≈1 kg). Why it works: mill pricing carries size/grade extras and small-lot premiums of a few % that disappear with larger, fewer orders; stamping plants nest more parts per coil. Benchmark: Xiaomi YU7's framework is built predominantly (90.2%) from high-strength steel and aluminium alloys – a mixed material body where grade discipline drives cost.

title: Mirror-symmetric LH/RH front-structure pressings halve unique part numbers
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Six die sets (or double-attached die halves) are not bought, part-number overhead and racks halve for those parts, and doubled batch sizes cut changeovers. Baseline: of ~10 handed front-structure parts (upper rail reinforcements, apron closers, crush-can backing plates, shock-tower caps, radiator-support side brackets, wheelhouse inner patches), every one is LH/RH-specific, produced either in separate dies or double-attached dies, with separate part numbers, racks and line-side presentation. Asymmetry usually comes from small features – a steering-rack clearance notch, a battery-cable (MHEV 12/48 V) clip hole, a brake-booster/ iBooster bracket hole. Proposal: redesign six of them to be identical LH and RH – symmetric about their own axis or flip-usable – by moving asymmetric features onto bolt-on brackets or making holes 'superset' (both sides pierced, unused hole plugged by adhesive patch or left as drain). The remaining four stay handed where geometry truly differs. Why it works: one part used twice doubles volume per die (100,000/yr instead of 50,000), halves part numbers and tooling, and lets steering-side-specific content live on cheap bolt-on parts. Benchmark: the 2025 Tesla Model Y reduced the number of unique parts at the front to simplify assembly and repair when it dropped the front casting.

title: Cavity wax confined to steel-aluminium interfaces in an aluminium-intensive body
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Less wax material per body, fewer spray-lance passes and shorter drip/flash time; cleaner downstream trim because less wax contaminates grommets, clips and adhesive bond faces. Baseline: cavity-wax flooding or spraying is applied to all body cavities (sills, pillars, rails, doors, tailgate) at roughly 1.2-1.8 kg per vehicle, carried over from steel-body practice, even where an aluminium body has cavities in 5xxx/6xxx alloys that do not suffer red-rust perforation. Proposal: map every cavity by material pair and exposure: (a) keep wax only at steel-aluminium interfaces (galvanic couples at steel hinge/latch reinforcements, steel inserts, hot-stamped parts joined to aluminium), at hem flanges and in sills below the wade line, (b) delete wax in Al-Al cavities above the wade line, relying on pre-treatment + E-coat + adhesive-sealed joints. Target 50-60% wax reduction and fewer spray-lance programs. Why it works: aluminium forms a passive oxide; the risks in an Al body are galvanic and filiform corrosion at interfaces and crevices – exactly where wax is kept. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460's MLA-Flex body is predominantly riveted and bonded sheet aluminium with cast sections, and its subframes are aluminium, reducing corrosion concerns.

ideaData.title: Cavity wax confined to steel-aluminium interfaces in an aluminium-intensive body
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: cavity-wax flooding or spraying is applied to all body cavities (sills, pillars, rails, doors, tailgate) at roughly 1.2-1.8 kg per vehicle, carried over from steel-body practice, even where an aluminium body has cavities in 5xxx/6xxx alloys that do not suffer red-rust perforation. Proposal: map every cavity by material pair and exposure: (a) keep wax only at steel-aluminium interfaces (galvanic couples at steel hinge/latch reinforcements, steel inserts, hot-stamped parts joined to aluminium), at hem flanges and in sills below the wade line, (b) delete wax in Al-Al cavities above the wade line, relying on pre-treatment + E-coat + adhesive-sealed joints. Target 50-60% wax reduction and fewer spray-lance programs. Why it works: aluminium forms a passive oxide; the risks in an Al body are galvanic and filiform corrosion at interfaces and crevices – exactly where wax is kept. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460's MLA-Flex body is predominantly riveted and bonded sheet aluminium with cast sections, and its subframes are aluminium, reducing corrosion concerns.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Less wax material per body, fewer spray-lance passes and shorter drip/flash time; cleaner downstream trim because less wax contaminates grommets, clips and adhesive bond faces.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Wax booth spray programs reduced by ~half, cycle per body −20-30 s; robot lance count may drop by 1-2; wax consumption −0.6-1.0 kg/vehicle; booth cleaning interval extended.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Cavity map with a 'wax / no-wax' attribute on each cavity drawing; lance access holes and drains only where wax is kept; fewer wax-plugged drain holes and fewer access-hole plugs to fit.

Low = 2.4+0.8+0.3 = €3.5; high = 5.4+1.2+0.3 = €6.9. Net €3.5-€6.9 per vehicle × 50,000 vehicles/yr = €0.175M-€0.345M per year (estimate; amortisation over 7 years = 350,000 vehicles where stated).

title: Fe-tolerant AlSi10MnMg chemistry lets rear megacast run 50% secondary aluminium
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Half the casting's melt is bought at the secondary price instead of primary, a €0.3-0.45/kg spread on ~60 kg, less the extra melt-chemistry control and inspection. Baseline: rear megacasts are typically specified in primary-based AlSi10MnMg with Fe ≤0.15-0.20%, because iron forms brittle needle-shaped β-Al5FeSi that cuts elongation – which forces primary ingot at a premium of roughly €0.3-0.45/kg over secondary-based melt. Proposal: re-specify the rear underbody casting (≈60 kg, not a frontal crush member) to a secondary-tolerant window: Fe 0.30-0.40% with Mn adjusted to Mn:Fe ≥ 0.5 (Mn 0.5-0.7%) so iron precipitates as compact 'Chinese-script' α-Al15(Fe,Mn)3Si2, Sr 80-150 ppm for eutectic modification, Cu ≤0.2% for corrosion, Zn ≤0.1%; as-cast/T7 target Rp0.2 ≥120 MPa, A ≥7% (vs ~10% primary), which the rear floor's stiffness-driven load cases accept. Charge with 50% post-consumer/process scrap. Why it works: Mn:Fe ratio control converts the harmful Fe phase; ductility loss is limited and confined to a part sized by stiffness, not energy absorption. Benchmark: Volvo states its megacasting will raise secondary (scrap) aluminium use, expected to reach 50% of content.

title: In-cell remelt of megacast biscuits, runners and overflows closes the return loop
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Avoids the remelter's toll spread and freight on ~30 kg of returns per casting; in-house melt cost (energy, dross, degassing) is lower than the spread. Baseline: a megacast shot weighs ~1.3-1.4× the finished casting; the biscuit, runners, overflows and X-ray rejects (≈25-35 kg per casting) are trimmed, bundled and sold back to an external remelter, then bought back as ingot – losing a toll/conversion spread of roughly €0.35-0.55/kg plus transport. Proposal: keep returns in the cell: hot-trimmed returns (still ~300 °C) are chopped in a trim-press shear and charged directly into a shaft/tower melting furnace beside the holding furnace, followed by rotary-impeller degassing (Ar/N2) to ≤0.10 ml/100 g H2, ceramic-foam filtration (30 ppi) and K-mould inclusion checks per shift; returns ratio in the charge capped at ~40% to hold chemistry. Melt loss target ≤3%. Why it works: return material is already in-specification alloy – remelting it in-house only costs fuel and dross loss, whereas the external loop pays margin twice; charging hot returns also cuts energy per kg. Benchmark: Volvo describes its megacasting approach as a zero-waste process.

title: Rear megacast nominal wall 3.5 → 2.8 mm with rib lattice saves 5-7 kg
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Aluminium and casting conversion are priced roughly per kilogram, so 5-7 kg less metal per casting is a direct saving; lower shot weight also shortens solidification. Baseline: first-generation rear underbody megacasts often run a 3.0-4.0 mm nominal wall (≈3.5 mm) for fill safety and stiffness, with ribs added where CAE showed weakness – leaving large lightly stressed panels heavier than needed. Proposal: drop the nominal wall to 2.8 mm on panels whose von Mises stress under all load cases (rear impact, towing D-value 16.7 kN, damper and sub-frame loads) is <40% of Rp0.2, and restore panel stiffness with a 2.0-2.5 mm rib lattice (40-60 mm pitch, 15-25 mm high) placed by topology optimisation; keep 3.5-5 mm at bosses, flanges and load nodes. Fill is secured by high vacuum (<50 mbar), overflow redesign, and gate velocity 40-60 m/s. Why it works: panel bending stiffness grows with rib height cubed, so a lattice recovers stiffness at far lower mass than uniform wall; mass falls ~8-12% of the casting. Benchmark: Tesla's 2025 Model Y rear casting redesign shed 7 kg.

title: Crushed-end tube with pierced tabs bolts to hinge and lock faces, deleting end brackets
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Two stamped brackets and two welds per beam are removed; the flattening is an extra stroke in an existing forming tool; bolting replaces welding inside the door-in-white line. Baseline: a tubular side-intrusion member (Ø28-32 mm martensitic or press-hardened tube) is usually MIG- or laser-welded at each end to a stamped HC420LA bracket (1.5-2.0 mm), and the brackets are then spot-welded or riveted to the hinge-face and lock-face of the inner panel – three parts and four joins per tube. Proposal: form the beam ends integrally: for a tube, flatten (crush) each end in the forming tool to a 30 × 60 mm double-wall tab before hardening, pierce 2 × Ø9 holes and fix with M8 10.9 bolts plus a structural adhesive pad to the hinge and lock reinforcements; for an open-hat beam, form the end flanges in the same hot-stamping hit. Brackets and their welds are deleted; tube mass is unchanged ±50 g. Why it works: under side load the tube bends and then pulls taut, so its ends see mostly axial pull and shear – two M8 10.9 bolts (≈2 × 30 kN preload, shear capacity >60 kN) plus an adhesive pad carry that; the crushed double wall doubles bearing thickness under the bolt heads, and the crush is done soft (before quench) so no cracking at the fold. Benchmark: Xiaomi YU7 fits 2,200 MPa ultra-high-strength steel anti-collision beams in all four doors.

title: Collapse self-piercing rivet catalogue to four lengths and two die profiles
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Higher volume per rivet variant brings unit-price reductions; fewer dedicated guns and feeders are needed; fewer changeovers and line stops for rivet/die mismatches. Baseline: an aluminium-intensive luxury SUV body uses ~2,200-2,800 self-piercing rivets drawn from 10-16 rivet variants (lengths 3.5-7.0 mm in 0.5 mm steps, two head diameters, two hardness classes, two coatings) and 15-25 die profiles, so many SPR guns are dedicated to one rivet/die pair and feeders cannot be shared. Proposal: re-qualify the body's joint stack-ups to four rivet lengths (4.0 / 5.0 / 6.0 / 6.5 mm), one head diameter (Ø7.75 head, Ø5.3 shank class), one hardness class and one zinc-tin coating, with two die profiles (flat for thin bottom sheets, pip die for thick); stack-ups that fall outside are redesigned (gauge rounding to 0.1 mm) or flagged. Why it works: SPR joint quality is governed by interlock and bottom thickness, which have a tolerance window wide enough that one rivet length covers ~1.2-1.5 mm of total stack variation; consolidation increases per-variant volume ~3-4×, earning price breaks, and lets guns serve more joints. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460's MLA-Flex is a riveted and bonded sheet-aluminium body with cast sections – SPR-intensive by design.

Why it works: SPR joint quality is governed by interlock and bottom thickness, which have a tolerance window wide enough that one rivet length covers ~1.2-1.5 mm of total stack variation; consolidation increases per-variant volume ~3-4×, earning price breaks, and lets guns serve more joints. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460's MLA-Flex is a riveted and bonded sheet-aluminium body with cast sections – SPR-intensive by design.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Higher volume per rivet variant brings unit-price reductions; fewer dedicated guns and feeders are needed; fewer changeovers and line stops for rivet/die mismatches.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: ~4 SPR guns removed or redeployed through joint re-allocation; feeder and spares inventory cut; joint-quality audits (cross-sections) reduced to fewer joint families.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Joint catalogue in CAD constrained to the approved rivet set; robot programs simplified; error-proofing improves because the same rivet appears on adjacent stations.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Medium – consumable price and gun count
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Low: 2,200 rivets × €0.03 × 5% price reduction = €3.3 + gun capex avoided €0.6M ÷ 350,000 = €1.7 + changeover/downtime €0.5 = €5.5. High: 2,800 × €0.032 × 8% = €7.2 + €1.7 + €1.0 = €9.9. Net €5.5-€9.9 per vehicle × 50,000 vehicles/yr = €0.275M-€0.495M per year (estimate; amortisation over 7 years = 350,000 vehicles where stated).

ideaData.riskNotes: Marginal interlock or bottom thickness for stacks at the edge of a rivet's window; corrosion with coating change. Validate: cross-section metrology per DVS 3410, ISO 14273/14272 coupons, VDA 233-102, full-vehicle torsion. Mitigate by redesigning outlier stacks rather than stretching windows.

title: Closure inners in EN AW-6016 to match outers, enabling closed-loop clean scrap
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Closed-loop clean 6016 scrap earns a higher credit than mixed 5xxx/6xxx offal on ~13-15 kg of closure offal per vehicle; bake-hardening allows no gauge increase in most panels. Baseline: aluminium closures typically pair a 6016-T4 (or 6014-T4) outer, 0.9-1.1 mm, with a 5182-O inner, 1.0-1.2 mm, chosen for deep-draw formability. Inners have large cut-outs (window, speaker, module openings), so 40-55% of inner blank mass becomes offal; because 5xxx (Mg ~4.5%) contaminates 6xxx, mixed offal is sold as lower-value mixed scrap rather than returned to the sheet mill as clean 6xxx. Proposal: switch bonnet, tailgate and four door inners to 6016-T4 at 1.1-1.2 mm (or a high-formability 6xxx variant where needed), redesigning inners for ≤10 mm shallower draws, radii ≥3t and spread draw beads; all closure offal then returns as segregated 6016 in a closed loop at a better credit. The inner also paint-bake hardens (+40-60 MPa), offsetting the formability compromise. Why it works: shallow-draw inner geometry is mostly flat panel with stiffening beads – within 6016-T4 limits (r ~0.6, n ~0.23) – and single-alloy offal is worth a premium to the mill. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460 is built from riveted and bonded sheet aluminium with cast sections.

title: Cast lift-and-jack receptacles in BEV sill end nodes replace bolted jacking pads
description: [800V BEV] [Off-road] Four jacking pads, eight to twelve bolts and their final-assembly fitting are deleted; casting the sockets into existing nodes adds only a small mass and a one-off die feature cost. Baseline: on a BEV with a full-width pack the workshop lift and jacking points must avoid the pack, so OEMs typically bolt four stamped or forged steel jacking pads (S420MC 3-4 mm, 2-3 M10 bolts each) to the sill extrusion at the front and rear ends, and off-road use (high-lift jack, recovery) has no defined point at all. Proposal: integrate the jacking receptacles into the four aluminium sill end nodes that already exist as castings (AlSi10MnMg, front and rear of the pack): a 40 × 40 mm square socket with 6 mm walls and a 70 × 70 mm bearing face, sized for 1.5 × max axle load per point (~22-25 kN) and marked by a cast-in symbol; the socket accepts the on-board jack, a workshop lift adapter and an off-road jack adapter. Pads, bolts and their fitting are deleted. Why it works: the end nodes sit on the sill-to-floor load path, so jack loads flow straight into the body without passing the pack frame; a socket also prevents the jack head slipping on uneven off-road ground. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460's MLA-Flex body uses cast aluminium sections, and an electric Range Rover has been driven off road ahead of launch, keeping off-road use a BEV requirement.

title: High-modulus PU windscreen adhesive lets cowl-to-A-pillar corner gussets be deleted
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Two gussets, their pressings and ~14 joints per vehicle are deleted; the higher-grade adhesive costs a little more per bead but far less than the steel/aluminium parts and joining. Baseline: standard 1K moisture-curing polyurethane windscreen adhesive has a low shear modulus (a few MPa), so the windscreen contributes little to aperture shear stiffness; bodies therefore add two cowl-to-A-pillar corner gussets (1.5 mm HSLA or 2.0 mm EN AW-5754, ~0.4-0.6 kg each, 6-8 joints each) to reach torsion and first front-end bending-mode targets. Proposal: specify a high-modulus, fast-cure PU glazing adhesive with shear modulus ≥3× the standard grade, a controlled 8 × 12 mm triangular bead and a primerless glass/frit system, and model the bonded windscreen as a structural shear panel in the body CAE; delete both corner gussets once the full-body torsion and front-end mode targets are met with glass fitted. Why it works: a 5-6 mm laminated windscreen bonded around its ~5 m perimeter is a stiff shear panel; raising the bond modulus increases how much aperture shear it carries, recovering the local stiffness the gussets supplied. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460's MLA-Flex body reaches 33 kNm/deg static torsional stiffness, up to 50% stiffer than its predecessor – the stiffness level the deletion must hold.

title: Elastomer duckbill door-drain valves keep wading water out of door cavities
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes door-bottom foam baffles and tape and reduces door water-ingress warranty claims after wading, at the cost of three small moulded valves per door sharing one part number. Baseline: door-bottom drain slots (2-3 per door) are left open so rain water inside the door can escape; in a 900 mm wade the door cavity floods through the same slots up to wading depth, wetting the door module, speaker and latch harness, so OEMs add foam baffles or tape at the door bottom and accept some water-ingress warranty after deep wading. Proposal: standardise the drains to Ø18 mm round holes and fit snap-in TPV (or EPDM) duckbill valves: the valve opens under ≥5 mm internal water head to drain, and closes under external hydrostatic pressure (a 900 mm wade gives ≈5-9 kPa at the door bottom); three valves per door, one part number for all doors. Delete the bottom foam baffle and tape. Why it works: a duckbill is a check valve whose lips are pressed shut by external pressure, so the drainage function and wading seal are no longer in conflict. Benchmark: the Range Rover L460 is rated for 900 mm wading with Wade Mode and Wade Sensing.

title: Printed hot-spot die segments cut megacast solidification time and shrinkage-pore scrap
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Shorter megacast cycle cuts press-hours per casting in the most expensive cell in the body plant, and fewer porosity rejects save whole castings; insert replacement is the offset. Baseline: megacast dies are cooled by straight drilled channels and jet coolers; thick nodes (damper towers, sub-frame bosses, towbar node) become hot spots that set the cycle (~100-120 s) and cause shrinkage porosity that drives X-ray/CT rejects of a few percent. Proposal: replace 6-8 die segments under the thick nodes with printed 1.2709 maraging or H11-type segments (HIP'd) whose water passages (Ø6 mm, 10-12 mm under the cavity) were positioned by adjoint optimisation, and pair them with pressure-controlled point coolers. Target: shot-to-shot time −12-15 s and CT/X-ray rejects −1 to −2 percentage points. Printed segments are treated as consumables (replaced roughly yearly) because they heat-check sooner than wrought steel. Why it works: per Chvorinov's rule the freezing time of a node scales with (volume/surface)², so extracting heat locally at the thick bosses shortens the whole shot and removes the last-to-freeze shrinkage pores that drive scrap. Benchmark: published research optimises conformal channel position and cross-section for 3D-printed tool-steel inserts in aluminium die casting and notes mould cooling can be up to 80% of die-casting cycle time.

title: Overspray-free contrast roof by nozzle-plate applicator, masking line deleted
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Removes manual masking labour and consumables, the second clearcoat application and the second oven pass for two-tone bodies, and the contrast paint lost as overspray (≈30-40% at bells). Also frees the off-line two-tone loop capacity that today caps the take rate. Baseline: luxury-SUV contrast (black or silver) roofs are painted in a second pass — body is fully painted, baked, then manually masked (tape + masking film along the roof ditch, DLO and pillars), sprayed with contrast basecoat + 2K clearcoat by rotary bells at 60-70% transfer efficiency, baked again and de-masked; masking and de-masking alone take about 50 minutes of operator time per body. Proposal: apply the contrast colour in the main topcoat line with a nozzle-plate (overspray-free) applicator: several dozen ≈0.1 mm nozzles, individually switchable, laying parallel paint jets from about 25 mm stand-off so the colour edge is sharp without tape. Route: body colour basecoat → flash → contrast basecoat jetted on roof (≈120 s) → common clearcoat → single bake, i.e. wet-on-wet two-tone in one pass. Transfer efficiency approaches 100% on the roof area (~3.2 m²). Benchmark: Dürr EcoPaintJet Pro is in series use for two-tone roofs; Dürr quotes ~120 s for a contrast roof versus ~50 min just to fix and remove masking tape. Note: BMW Debrecen (Neue Klasse, iX3) shows the wider move to dry-separation booths

title: Windscreen black-band projection display replaces instrument-cluster TFT and hood
description: [800V BEV] Removes the cluster TFT module (display, backlight, cover glass, PCB, housing), the binnacle hood moulding and wrap, and their harness branch; the added content is a print pattern on the existing frit operation, a local p-pol coating and one PGU. Baseline: a luxury SUV carries a 12.3-in instrument-cluster TFT with its own housing, cover lens, binnacle hood (soft-skin or wrapped) and a separate optional combiner-free windscreen HUD with wedge PVB. Proposal (BEV first, MHEV at facelift): delete the cluster TFT and binnacle hood and present driving information on a black ceramic-enamel band printed on the lower windscreen inner face (#4) from A-pillar to A-pillar, illuminated by a wide picture-generation unit under the IP top pad. The black band is printed and fired in the same screen-print/bending cycle as the perimeter frit, so it adds a print pattern, not a process. A p-polarised reflective coating on the band area gives a single image with polarised sunglasses and removes the wedge-PVB need for that zone. The main road-facing HUD can remain as an option on the same glass. Benchmark: BMW Panoramic Vision (iX3 Neue Klasse, 2025) projects content onto a black printed surface across the lower windscreen from A-pillar to A-pillar, and the iX3 replaces the traditional dashboard cluster with it; AGC supplies a black-band display solution with a proprietary p-polarised coat

title: Split front bumper: replaceable unpainted corner modules on common centre fascia
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Off-road variant changes only two small corner tools instead of a full-width fascia tool; corners need no paint; in-plant paint scrap on the big fascia falls because the painted area shrinks by ≈30%; warranty/goodwill and dealer-repair claims for corner damage replace a €45 corner instead of a €200+ painted fascia. Baseline: one-piece painted front fascia (≈1.9 m wide, 5.5 kg PP-EPDM-TD20, painted base + 2K clear) with an off-road-pack variant that raises the lower corners for approach angle — a second full-width tool and a separate paint SKU set. Any corner scrape on a trail means replacing and painting the whole fascia. Proposal: three-piece bumper — a painted centre fascia (common across all trims) plus left/right corner modules in mould-in-colour (MIC) grained PP-EPDM-TD15 with UV-stabilised black pigment, attached by a tongue-and-groove joint with 3 hidden clips and 2 M6 screws each side. Two corner tools: road corner (flush, lower) and off-road corner (cut up ≈60 mm at the wheel-arch lead-in, improving approach angle). Corner modules carry the wheel-arch air-curtain inlet and fog/side-marker pocket. Benchmark: Toyota Land Cruiser 250 (2024) uses a split bumper so only the corners — where off-road damage is most likely — are replaced, and cut the lower front and rear bumper down to avoid rocks.

title: Fixed tailgate wing and rear aero blades replace extending active spoiler
description: [800V BEV] Deletes the spoiler actuator, linkage, position sensing, ECU output stage, harness and seal; the fixed wing is a single moulding with integral high-mounted stop lamp pocket; less warranty exposure (ice-jam, actuator failure). Baseline for a premium BEV SUV chasing a low drag figure: an automatically extending rear roof spoiler — electric actuator with worm gear, 4-bar linkage, end-position sensing, a dedicated ECU channel, wiring, seal, and a PC/ABS painted blade — deploying above ≈90 km/h. Proposal: a fixed roof-trailing-edge wing in long-glass PP (PP-LGF30, painted or MIC black) whose chord and kick angle are set for the motorway case, plus two vertical rear-pillar aero blades that tidy the C-pillar separation and reduce wake width. Gurney height fixed at 8-10 mm, trailing edge 2 mm. The fixed solution removes mechanism and actuator; any small Cd penalty at low speed is irrelevant because aero load scales with speed². Benchmark: Polestar 3 reaches Cd 0.29 with a front aero wing integrated in the bonnet, a fixed rear aero wing on the liftgate and rear side aero blades; Porsche Macan Electric uses an automatically extending rear spoiler — the comparison shows a fixed package is viable on a large SUV.

title: One illuminated-grille hardware fit; animations sold as feature-on-demand
description: [800V BEV] Two of three hardware variants deleted: fewer PCB/mask tools, one validation and homologation file, one service part, simpler line-side sequencing; software-unlock revenue (not counted in the saving) offsets the slightly richer hardware on lower trims. Baseline: BEV luxury SUVs increasingly fit an illuminated grille/front signature in several hardware levels — a static contour light (base), a segmented animated version (mid) and a full animated pixel grille (top) — each with its own LED PCB, driver count, light-guide mask and harness pin-out: 3 hardware variants, 3 validation programmes and 3 service part numbers. Proposal: fit a single segmented-grille hardware set to every trim that has the illuminated option (one PCB layout, one light-guide/mask, one 2-wire CAN-FD or LIN driver node) and differentiate only in software: base trims run a static pattern, higher trims unlock welcome/goodbye animations and charging-state patterns over the air. Hardware is sized at the mid level (≈140 LEDs) with the mask creating the high apparent pixel count. Benchmark: Kia EV9 fits a Digital Pattern Lighting grille on upper trims and sells five additional lighting patterns as a US$250 software unlock; BMW X5 LCI offers Iconic Glow contour lighting as a pack option; Mercedes GLC with EQ Technology lights 942 grille dots with 140 LEDs.

title: Wing-cavity high air intake gives 900 mm wading without snorkel variant
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] Deletes the snorkel accessory engineering/validation and the A-pillar BIW mounting provisions on every body; deletes the water-separator plenum (inlet is above wading line); avoids splash-guard and grille duct seal on the MHEV front end. Baseline: the 3.0 L I6 MHEV draws air through a grille-level snout behind the headlamp (inlet ≈700-750 mm above ground), so 900 mm wading needs a water-separating plenum with a duckbill drain valve and, for markets that want more margin, a separately engineered raised-intake (snorkel) accessory with its own A-pillar mounting holes and validation. Proposal: move the primary inlet into the front-wing upper cavity behind the headlamp, with the opening under the bonnet shut-line (inlet ≥ 1,050 mm ground clearance at standard ride height, ≥ 1,125 mm in off-road height). The duct is a two-shell PP-T20 blow/inject part running down the wing cavity to the airbox; a labyrinth in the bonnet shut-line drain channel rejects rain, and the airbox keeps one drain valve. The snorkel accessory and its body-in-white provisions are dropped. Benchmark: Land Rover states its Defender raised air intake accessory does not extend wading beyond the standard 900 mm, i.e. the standard intake already meets the brand wading figure; BYD Yangwang U8 needs a snorkel to go from 1,000 mm to 1,400 mm wading on its Off-road Master edition.

title: Illuminated grille light-guide plate: 140 LEDs light 942 dots
description: [800V BEV] LED count −70%, driver ICs −50-60%, PCB area −60% and a reflector-cell grid deleted; the light-guide plate is one injection-moulded or cut-and-etched part. Baseline approach for a "pixel" illuminated grille: one LED per visible cell or per pair of cells — ≈450-500 mid-power LEDs on 4 FR4 boards, 6-8 constant-current driver ICs, a reflector-cell grid and a diffuser film behind the mask. Proposal: an edge- and back-lit light-guide architecture: 140 LEDs on two aluminium-core strips along the top and bottom of the grille, coupling into a 4 mm PMMA light-guide plate with laser-etched or printed extraction dots registered to the 942 openings of an opaque PC/ASA mask (or chrome-look PVD on the mask face). Each LED feeds ≈6-7 apparent pixels; animation is done in zones (groups of LEDs), not per pixel. Extraction dot density is graded with distance from the LED to equalise luminance (target uniformity ≥ 0.7 min/max). Benchmark: Mercedes-Benz GLC with EQ Technology (2025) illuminates 942 small grille squares with 140 individual LEDs.

title: Indirect rear light bar reflected off textured garnish replaces light-guide bar
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Removes the PMMA light guide, its LED coupling engines, the outer lens, the welded housing and its seal; the textured garnish is a part the tailgate already carries, gaining a micro-texture in its tool. Baseline: a full-width (≈1.3-1.5 m) direct-view tailgate light bar — PMMA rod/blade light guide fed by LED engines at each end (plus mid-span boosters for uniformity), a diffuser, a red PMMA outer lens, a 2-shot housing, vent membrane and vibration-welded seal. It is a separate lamp with its own photometry, sealing and stone-chip exposure. Proposal: make the bar a signature/position lamp that shines indirectly: a linear LED strip on a slim aluminium-core PCB is hidden upward under the tailgate spoiler lip / garnish overhang and illuminates a moulded micro-textured red-tinted garnish surface (PC/ASA with moulded micro-facets), which reflects and scatters the light rearward. No light guide, no outer lens, no welded housing — the PCB sits in a sealed snap-in channel with a clear PC cover. Regulatory stop/tail/turn stay in the corner lamps. Benchmark: Tesla Model Y "Juniper" (2025) uses an indirect rear running light: the bar is tucked upward and its red light is reflected down onto a custom-textured strip; Tesla described it as an industry first.

title: RGB light-bar segments show charge status; charge-port LED module deleted
description: [800V BEV] Deletes one or two charge-port LED modules, their light guides, connectors and harness branches (and a CAN/LIN node if separate); light-bar segment LEDs are re-specified once. Baseline: BEVs indicate charge state with a dedicated LED ring or bar in the charge-port housing (RGB LEDs, small PCB, light guide, connector and harness branch on each charge port — often two ports on a luxury SUV: AC and DC or both sides). Proposal: drive the front and rear signature light bars with RGB (or W + amber + green) segmented LED channels split into 10 segments, so charge state is shown in 10% steps visible from outside the car; delete the charge-port status LEDs and their harness branches. The segment controller already exists for welcome animation; add a charging-state message from the on-board charger/BMS to the lighting zone controller. Hazard "drive-around" amber graphics can reuse the same segments when stationary. Benchmark: Rivian R1S Gen 2 (2025) light bars use new RGB colour-changing LEDs split into ten segments that show battery charging status in green 10% increments front and rear, plus animated amber graphics.

title: Mirror head: wade transducer, puddle lamp and indicator on one LIN board
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes the dedicated wade-sensing ECU, three pigtails/connectors per mirror and 8-10 harness circuits through the door; one PCB replaces three small boards. Baseline: an off-road luxury SUV mirror head contains up to five separate electrical items — glass heater, fold motor, turn-indicator module, puddle/logo-projector lamp and a downward-facing ultrasonic wade-sensing transducer — each with its own pigtail and connector into a 12-16-way mirror harness; wade sensing is processed in a dedicated control unit. Proposal: one rigid-flex PCB in the mirror base carries the 40-58 kHz ultrasonic transducer driver, the puddle-lamp LED with its gobo optic, the turn-indicator LED string and a LIN slave that also drives the fold motor H-bridge; the mirror harness drops to 4 wires (12 V, ground, LIN, heater feed) plus the camera coax. Echo time-of-flight is computed locally and sent as water-depth over LIN to the body zone controller, which runs the wade-depth HMI — deleting the separate wade ECU. Benchmark: Land Rover Wade Sensing uses ultrasonic sensors fitted in the exterior mirrors facing downward; a control unit calculates water depth corrected for vehicle pitch and shows it against the maximum wading depth (900 mm on Range Rover).

title: Rear wheel-arch flare with moulded-in air-curtain channel, duct deleted
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes the separate curtain duct, its seal and bracket and 3-4 clips per side; the flare tool gains a slide and a small cover tool; one install instead of two. Baseline: where a luxury SUV uses rear air curtains to clean up flow behind the rear wheels, the curtain is a separate PP blow-moulded duct clipped behind the bumper or flare with a foam seal, plus a bracket, while the wheel-arch flare (off-road protective cladding) is a separate MIC PP-EPDM moulding with 8-10 clips. Proposal: integrate the air curtain into the flare itself — the flare is moulded as an outer skin with a 6-8 mm deep channel on its B-side, closed by a short inner cover vibration-welded (or hot-plate welded) to the flare, forming an inlet slot at the leading edge of the flare and an exit slot on the arch face that blows across the rear tyre sidewall. The flare stays mould-in-colour PP-EPDM-TD15 (UV-black, grained) so stone and branch scuffs off-road need no paint repair. Benchmark: Mercedes-Benz G 580 with EQ Technology (2024) adds "air curtains" in the rear wheel-arch flares, together with A-pillar cladding and a roof spoiler lip, to optimise aerodynamics on the electric G.

title: Common tailgate carrier hosts spare wheel or BEV cable-storage box
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] One tailgate inner/reinforcement and one carrier tool family across powertrains; BEV cable storage moves outside the cabin, removing a separate frunk/load-floor cable compartment moulding; fewer tailgate part numbers in body-shop sequencing. Baseline: an off-road luxury SUV with a side-hinged or drop tailgate offers an external spare wheel on a powertrain-specific carrier (MHEV) while the BEV — which must package charging cables and often loses the underfloor spare well to the rear motor — gets a different tailgate reinforcement and a frunk or load-floor cable bag. Proposal: one tailgate inner reinforcement and one 3-point carrier interface (M12 studs on a hot-formed 22MnB5 AS150 carrier plate) common to both powertrains; three bolt-on heads: (a) spare-wheel carrier (MHEV and off-road packs), (b) lockable PP-LGF30 cable-storage box styled as a wheel cover with drain holes and IP54 lid seal (BEV), (c) flat design cover. Carrier is rated for a 35 kg wheel at 6 g vertical abuse so the box (≈6 kg with cables) is far inside its envelope. Benchmark: Mercedes-Benz G 580 with EQ Technology offers a rear "design box" styled like a spare-wheel cover that stores the charging cables, and buyers choose between rear design cover, design box or spare wheel.

title: Wedge-free HUD windscreen using p-polarised reflective coating
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Wedge acoustic PVB premium removed on every HUD windscreen; one PVB type and one lamination recipe for all windscreens, cutting PVB inventory and changeover scrap at the glass supplier. Baseline: windscreens for head-up display use a wedge-shaped acoustic PVB (wedge angle ≈0.3-0.6 mrad) so the reflections from the inner and outer glass surfaces overlap and do not form a ghost image; HUD and non-HUD vehicles therefore need two different interlayers, two lamination recipes and two part numbers, and wedge acoustic PVB costs a large premium over standard acoustic PVB. The s-polarised HUD image also disappears with polarised sunglasses. Proposal: switch the HUD to p-polarised projection and add a thin reflective coating in the HUD patch on the glass inner ply (#3 or #4). Near Brewster angle (≈56-57° for soda-lime), the bare glass surfaces reflect almost no p-polarised light, so the coating provides the single image and the ghost from the outer surface vanishes without a wedge. All windscreens then use the same flat acoustic PVB; HUD variants add only the coating patch. Benchmark: AGC has a proprietary p-polarised coating already adopted in its Windshield Black-Band Display and keeps HUD content visible with polarised sunglasses; Saint-Gobain has patented HUD windshields with p-polarisation reflection coatings.

title: Headlamp housing with moulded air-curtain channel replaces fascia ducts
description: [800V BEV] Two ducts, two gaskets and 6-8 clips deleted; the headlamp housing gains a channel geometry in an existing tool (slide action), and one sealing interface replaces two. Baseline: front air curtains on a luxury SUV are fed by inlets in the lower fascia corners and two separate PP-T20 ducts (each with a foam gasket and 3-4 clips) running round the headlamp to an exit slot in front of the front wheel. Proposal: route the channel through the headlamp's own lower carrier: the headlamp housing (PP-TD/PP-GF lower carrier for weight, PC lens unchanged) is moulded with an open U-channel on its outboard face, closed by the fascia corner skin, with an inlet under the DRL and an exit at the wheel-arch lip. The fascia corner seals onto the channel with a co-moulded TPE lip on the housing. On the BEV the closed front means cooling inlets are small, so the outboard space is available. Benchmark: Xiaomi YU7 (2025) headlamps use a hollowed water-drop design with full-length integrated air channels; Porsche Macan Electric places air curtains below the headlight module.

title: One wheel casting for both powertrains; BEV range gained by snap-in PA6 face disc
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Removes a BEV-specific wheel casting die set, machining fixtures and paint programme; aluminium mass per wheel falls by the closed-face material; the cover is a low-cost injection moulding. Baseline: platform-shared MHEV/BEV luxury SUVs release separate wheel designs per powertrain: the BEV gets dedicated closed-face A356.2-T6 low-pressure castings (extra aluminium in the closed areas, ≈1-1.5 kg per rim, own die set, machining fixture and paint/diamond-cut programme), while MHEV keeps open designs — doubling die sets per size. Proposal: release one casting per size for both powertrains (same die, X-ray and machining programme) and give the BEV its range benefit with a snap-in face disc: PA6-GF30 (or PP-LGF30 for lower cost) moulding, painted or PVD-look, retained by 4 stainless spring clips into machined pockets on the rim back face plus the centre-cap lock. The disc closes 60-70% of the window area and leaves a perimeter gap for brake cooling. The disc is also an MHEV efficiency option and is removed for off-road use (mud packing). Benchmark: Range Rover Electric / Range Rover Sport Electric gain up to 16 km motorway range from an optimised grille plus aerodynamic alloys; Mercedes G 580 pairs its aero package with aero wheels.

title: Bonnet leading-edge aero wing replaces upper grille and cowl air-guide parts
description: [800V BEV] Deletes the blanked upper grille, air-guide moulding and one seal row; the under-wing moulding is a single simple part; leakage-drag reduction adds range for free (not counted in the saving). Baseline: on a closed-front BEV derived from an ICE body, the upper grille area is still filled with a blanked upper grille, a separate air-guide moulding behind it, and bonnet-to-fascia sealing rubbers to stop air leaking into the front compartment — 4-6 parts adding drag through leakage and steps. Proposal: form the bonnet leading edge as an aero wing — a ≈40 mm high slot between the bonnet front edge and the fascia top, with the bonnet outer flange (EN AW-6016-T4 outer, hemmed) shaped as the wing upper surface and a PP-LGF30 under-wing moulding clipped to the bonnet inner — that re-attaches flow onto the bonnet. The blanked upper grille and air-guide parts are deleted; the fascia top becomes a simple closed surface sealed to the front-end carrier. Benchmark: Polestar 3 (2024) has a front aero wing integrated into the bonnet that attaches air to the bonnet and improves laminar flow, contributing to Cd 0.29.

title: Segmented mini-LED rear lamp replaces six digital OLED panels
description: [800V BEV] Replaces OLED panels (cost driven by OLED deposition and encapsulation yield) with commodity mid-power red LEDs and a moulded baffle grid; removes OLED-specific thermal management and humidity protection. Baseline: top-trim premium BEVs use digital OLED rear lamps — e.g. six OLED panels per car with 60 segments each (360 segments) driven by a dedicated controller, used for selectable signatures and car-to-X warning symbols. OLED panels are expensive per lit area, sensitive to temperature and humidity (thin-film encapsulation) and need red-light lifetime margins. Proposal: keep the same function — ≈60 individually addressable segments per side — with a mini-LED array: mid-power red LEDs at 3-4 mm pitch on an aluminium-core PCB, a moulded micro-lens/baffle grid (PC) that defines each segment, and a volume-diffusing PMMA layer giving homogeneous, OLED-like appearance at 25-30 mm depth. Segments are driven by 16-channel matrix LED drivers on the same PCB, controlled from the lighting zone controller (CAN-FD). title: Flexible TPV rebound flap closes rear-wheel underbody gap
description: [800V BEV] Seal lip/second panel and its clips deleted; 2K moulding of the flap onto the panel replaces an assembly; flexible flap allows a fuller surface without clearance-driven extra parts. Baseline: the rigid underbody panel ahead of the rear wheel must leave ≈25-35 mm clearance to the tyre and link at full rebound/jounce and with snow chains, so it ends short, and a separate EPDM seal lip or a second small panel with 4-6 clips is added to partly close the gap — still leaving an open slot in rebound. Proposal: replace the panel tip and seal with one flexible flap injection-moulded in TPV (EPDM/PP, 75-85 Shore A, UV and ozone stabilised), 3.0 mm with moulded stiffening ribs, overmoulded (2K) onto the rigid PP-T20 panel edge or clipped in a single row. The flap closes the gap aerodynamically at normal ride height and simply deflects when the tyre/link approaches in rebound, chain fitment or off-road articulation. Benchmark: Porsche Macan Electric (2024) has flexible elements near the rear wheels that keep the underbody surface closed during the rebound phase of suspension travel, as part of its flat underbody reaching Cd 0.25.

title: Park sensors moved above bumper split line; lower valance unpainted and hole-free
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Lower valance paint deleted (base + clear on ≈0.35 m² per bumper); sensor bezel/holder variants and hole-punch operations for the lower area deleted; warranty and goodwill claims for off-road-damaged sensors and valances fall. Baseline: front and rear bumpers carry 12 ultrasonic park sensors, of which 4-6 sit in the painted lower valance close to the ground; off-road use (rock, ruts, wading) damages sensors and valance, and the painted lower valance with sensor holes needs per-colour paint, bezel parts and hole-punching variants. Proposal: relocate all ultrasonic sensors to the upper fascia above the main split line (sensor centre height ≥ 520 mm), re-angle them 3-5° downward to keep the low-obstacle detection cone, and make the lower valance a mould-in-colour grained PP-EPDM-TD15 (UV-black) part with no sensor holes, no paint and replaceable from below with 6 screws. Benchmark: on the Lexus GX 550 Overtrail (2024), the front bumper sensors are located above a main seam and the lower skid plate is removable — keeping the vulnerable lower area free of sensors.

title: Forged 42CrMo4 recovery eyes through crash-box flange delete tow-hook covers
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes the loose towing eye, its foam stowage, threaded boss, painted tow-hook cover and the off-road recovery-hook accessory kit; adds two/three forgings that double as the regulatory towing device. Baseline: luxury SUVs store a screw-in towing eye in the load floor, thread it into a welded M24 boss in the crash box behind a painted hinged tow-hook cover in the fascia (cover, hinge clip, paint per colour), and sell a separate bolt-on recovery-hook kit for the off-road pack. Proposal: fit permanent forged recovery eyes, front pair and one rear, in 42CrMo4+QT (Rm 1,000-1,200 MPa, closed-die forged, shot-peened, zinc-flake coated), bolted through the crash-box flange with two M14 10.9 bolts each and exposed through a small moulded aperture in the MIC lower valance — no cover flap, no screw-in eye, no off-road kit. Eye rated for ≥ 1.5 × GVW static pull at ±30° horizontal/±15° vertical. Benchmark: INEOS Grenadier comes standard with towing eyes front and rear and is rated for 3.5 t braked towing and 5.5 t winching, showing permanent recovery points as a standard off-road feature.

title: Gloss-black B/C-pillar appliqués deleted; pillars jet-painted black inline
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Removes 4-6 moulded appliqués, their hard-coat, adhesive tapes, primer and fitting labour; black paint on ≈0.4 m² costs a fraction; avoids appliqué warranty (fading, delamination, scratches). Baseline: the "floating roof" look on luxury SUVs is made with gloss-black pillar appliqués: 4-6 injection-moulded PMMA or PC/ASA parts (2.5-3 mm, high-gloss piano black, often with a scratch-resistant hard-coat) bonded with acrylic foam tape or clipped onto door frames and pillars. They need their own tools, hard-coat line, adhesion promoter and assembly, and they scratch and delaminate. Proposal: delete the appliqués on the door-frame B/C pillars and paint the pillar surfaces gloss black directly in the topcoat booth with the same overspray-free nozzle-plate applicator used for the contrast roof (black base, then common clearcoat — wet-on-wet), with a sharp design edge and no masking. Benchmark: Dürr's EcoPaintJet Pro (2022 update) can paint and apply design elements to complex vertical surfaces such as A- and C-pillars fully automatically and without masking.

title: Light-bar diffuser in volume-scattering PMMA replaces film + clear lens stack
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] One optical part instead of lens + diffuser film/moulding; lamination/assembly step deleted; dust-in-gap rejects eliminated; one tool instead of two per bar. Baseline: a full-width front or rear light bar with segment-level control (e.g. 10 segments) uses a clear PC or PMMA lens plus a separate diffuser film or a second diffuser moulding, sometimes with a printed or laminated pattern, to hide individual LEDs and give uniform segments — two optical parts, a lamination or assembly step, and a dust-sensitive gap between them. Proposal: a single 2.5-3.0 mm lens moulded in volume-scattering PMMA (light-diffusing grade with dispersed micro-particles, transmission ≈60-70%, haze > 90%) with moulded segment-separating ribs on the B-side; the outer face is hard-coated for scratch and UV resistance. LED pitch and stand-off (≈18-22 mm) are set so the segment uniformity ≥ 0.75 is met by the material itself. Benchmark: Rivian R1S Gen 2 (2025) redesigned its front and rear light bars to be more three-dimensional and split them into ten RGB segments — a light bar where segment uniformity and LED hiding are critical.

title: Tempered rear quarter and fixed door glass where laminate adds nothing
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Laminated small glasses cost roughly 1.8-2.2× tempered of the same size (two plies, PVB, autoclave cycle); tempered also saves ≈0.8-1.0 kg per car and shortens supplier lead time. Baseline: premium SUVs increasingly laminate all side glass (front and rear door drops, rear fixed door glass and rear quarter glass) for acoustics and intrusion resistance — typically 2.1 mm + 0.76 mm acoustic PVB + 2.1 mm (≈5 mm) versus 3.85-4.0 mm tempered. Proposal: keep laminated acoustic glass on front and rear door drop glasses (largest area, nearest occupants' ears) but specify the small fixed rear-door quarterlets and the body-side rear quarter glasses (each 0.10-0.25 m²) as 3.85 mm tempered with solar-tinted body, encapsulated in PVC-free TPE. Their acoustic contribution is small because transmitted sound power scales with area and they sit behind the C-pillar trim and third-row/luggage zone; an acoustic check by SEA or transfer-path analysis decides per window. Benchmark: Volvo EX90 laminates many of its windows (labelled with a laminated-glass symbol) for better sound insulation and safety — the baseline; the proposal right-sizes this per window.

title: Wade-sensor transducer snapped into mirror-base acoustic window, bracket deleted
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Removes bracket, two screws, decoupling ring and bezel per mirror; aim set by tooling instead of an adjustable bracket, deleting the aim check at mirror EOL. Baseline: a downward-facing ultrasonic wade-depth transducer in the mirror is held by a separate PA6-GF bracket screwed into the mirror base, with a decoupling ring and a painted or grained bezel to hide it. Proposal: mould the mirror base (PA6-GF30 or ASA/PC for the visible lower shell) with an integral cylindrical acoustic window — a 0.8-1.0 mm thin membrane-free aperture with a moulded snap cage and a 2K TPE decoupling collar (shot onto the base) — so the transducer snaps in from inside and is aimed vertically by the mould geometry (aim tolerance ±1°). Bezel, bracket, screws and separate decoupler deleted. Benchmark: Land Rover Wade Sensing uses ultrasonic sensors fitted in the exterior mirrors facing downward to measure the distance to the water surface.

title: Illuminated grille mask in laser-ablated black PC instead of chrome slats
description: [800V BEV] Electroplated slats and their clip assembly deleted; one moulding plus paint and laser ablation replaces 10-20 plated parts; radar cover integrated into the same skin. Baseline: a chrome-look closed BEV grille on a luxury SUV is built from electroplated ABS or PC/ABS slats/frame (Cu-Ni-Cr plating, 25-35 µm) clipped into a black PC/ABS carrier, often with a separate radar cover. Plating is the largest cost item and limits light transmission for illuminated designs. Proposal: one 3 mm PC (radar-compatible, low-loss grade) mask, back-painted or in-mould-decorated opaque black, with the 900-plus pattern openings created by laser ablation of the back paint (not by through-holes), so the front surface stays a single closed, cleanable, radar-transparent skin. Chrome look, where wanted, is a thin PVD indium/aluminium-free decorative layer only on raised frame features. The same mask works lit (backlight shows through ablated dots) or unlit. Benchmark: the Mercedes-Benz GLC with EQ Technology (2025) grille has 942 backlit squares lit by 140 LEDs, inspired by the chrome structures of classic Mercedes grilles — showing a lit dot pattern replacing physical chrome slats.

title: Roof-ditch moulding co-extruded with TPV protection strip for roof-load abuse
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Merges the ditch finisher and the protection strip into one extrusion; deletes metal spine and the separate bonded strip and its adhesive/primer step; one part number across trims. Baseline: a luxury SUV roof carries a separate roof-ditch finisher (PVC or TPE extrusion with an aluminium or steel retaining spine) and, on off-road packs, an additional bonded rubber roof-protection strip or accessory pads to protect paint from roof-tent, rack and load scuffs. Proposal: one co-extruded roof-ditch moulding: rigid PP-T20 or PVC-free polyolefin spine, an exposed TPV wear surface (75 Shore A, UV-stabilised, matt black) standing 2-3 mm proud of the roof skin to act as the protection strip, and a soft TPV sealing lip to the ditch walls; clipped into the ditch on the existing stud pattern. One profile for both trims; off-road pack simply uses the same moulding. Benchmark: INEOS Grenadier comes standard with roof rails and roof protection strips, and its optional roof rack is rated for 150 kg dynamic and 420 kg static load — showing roof-protection features as standard off-road content.

title: Rear underbody panels in compression-moulded PET fleece replace PP-T20 mouldings
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Aluminium compression tools cost ≈25-35% of steel injection tools; material cost per panel similar or lower; absorber felt deleted; mass saving ≈1.5-2 kg per car. Baseline: rear-zone underbody panels (rear axle area, either side of the spare well / rear e-motor, ≈1.2-1.6 m² total) injection-moulded in PP-T20 at 2.5-3.0 mm, ≈4.5-5.5 kg, plus separate absorber felt where tyre noise is an issue. Proposal: compression-moulded PET (or PET/co-PET bicomponent) nonwoven fleece at 1,200-1,500 g/m², heat-consolidated to 2.5-4 mm with locally fully-densified edges and fastener zones, hydrophobic and oleophobic finish. Process: needle-punched fleece → contact-heat to ≈200 °C → cold compression-mould in an aluminium tool (cycle 45-60 s) → waterjet trim. Mass ≈1.5-1.9 kg per m² → ≈40% lighter than PP-T20, and the porous structure absorbs tyre and e-motor noise so separate absorber pads are deleted. Benchmark: Porsche Macan Electric (2024) relies on a fully sealed underbody with flexible covers for Cd 0.25 — the proposal keeps the closed surface while changing the panel material.

ideaData.title: Right-size rear-wheel steering to ±5° with one MHEV/BEV central actuator
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: a flagship luxury SUV specifies a large rear-steer angle (Range Rover L460 reaches 7.3 deg for a sub-11 m turning circle). That angle sizes everything downstream: a central spindle actuator with ~±22-25 mm stroke, a rear knuckle and tie-rod geometry that must clear the 22-23 in wheel and liner at full lock, extra wheel-arch liner clearance, and a separate actuator calibration for each powertrain because MHEV and BEV rear axles carry different loads. Proposal: specify ±5 deg (Cayenne Electric uses up to 5 deg, GLC with EQ Technology 4.5 deg) and design ONE central actuator, one rear tie-rod pair and one knuckle steering-arm geometry for both the MHEV and 800V BEV rear subframes. Rack stroke falls ~30% (stroke scales roughly with tan of angle: tan5/tan7.3 = 0.68), so the ball-screw can be ~15 mm shorter, the BLDC motor drops one frame size (peak rack force at the smaller angle stays similar but required power at the same slew rate falls with stroke), and the housing shortens. Turning-circle loss is recovered at the front: the 5 deg rear angle still delivers most of the low-speed agility (rear-steer benefit is near-linear in angle while tyre scrub and liner clearance rise faster). Same actuator part number across both powertrains doubles its volume to 50,000/yr.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Shorter ball-screw and housing, one-frame-smaller motor and power stage, smaller rear liner/clearance features and one shared actuator and tie-rod part number for MHEV and BEV instead of two calibrated variants; volume pooling lowers piece price and halves validation.
