title: Tubular passive bars and dual-chamber air delete 48 V roll control on BEV
description: [800V BEV] Deletes two eARC actuators, their 48 V power electronics, harness and the extra 48 V DC/DC capacity on BEV volume trims; passive hollow bars and drop-links cost a fraction. Removes ~20 kg, which also helps range. Baseline: the platform fits 48 V electronic active roll control (two actuators + power electronics + 48 V supply from the DC/DC) to all trims, as Range Rover L460 does. On the 800V BEV the 100-115 kWh pack sits under the floor, lowering the centre of gravity by roughly 60-100 mm versus the MHEV; roll moment (m·a·h) falls proportionally (~10-15% for the same roll-centre heights), so the body-roll gradient target can be met passively. Proposal: on BEV volume trims replace eARC with tubular passive bars (front 34MnB5 tube Ø30 x 4.5 mm, rear Ø24 x 3.5 mm, quenched and tempered, shot-peened, e-coated) tuned together with the dual-chamber air spring in its stiff (small-volume) setting, which adds vertical and roll stiffness on demand. Polestar 3 engineers state its dual-chamber air suspension and torque-vectoring rear drive make active anti-roll unnecessary; on our BEV twin-motor torque split adds the yaw tuning. eARC stays on the performance BEV and on the MHEV (higher CoG, towing).

title: Chassis domain controller absorbs air-suspension, damper and rear-steer ECUs
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Three ECU housings, PCBs, MCUs, connectors and CAN nodes deleted; one larger controller added. Harness shortens (fewer ECU-to-ECU runs). One software stack and one calibration toolchain instead of four supplier stacks reduces engineering and OTA cost. Baseline: a typical luxury SUV carries separate controllers for air-suspension levelling, continuous damping control, rear-wheel steering and active roll, each with its own housing, connector, CAN-FD node, bootloader, calibration and supplier software, plus the ESC/brake ECU. Proposal: move all chassis motion-control algorithms (levelling, skyhook damping, RWS angle, roll moment distribution) into one chassis domain controller and keep only "smart" power stages at the actuators (valve drivers in the air-supply unit, damper valve drivers clustered in two zone drivers, motor inverters inside the RWS and eARC actuators). BMW iX3 Neue Klasse does this with its "Heart of Joy" central controller, which handles propulsion, braking, recuperation, torque distribution and steering sub-functions at 1,000 cycles per second, about ten times the previous control units. Our version need not include propulsion: a 6-core lockstep MCU (ASIL-D) with 8 MB flash runs the four functions, removing three standalone ECUs and the inter-ECU signal latency (single loop typically improves damper-to-roll coordination by 10-20 ms).

title: Single brake actuation architecture across MHEV and BEV via common one-box
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] MHEV loses the electric pump, hoses/check valve, pneumatic assistance unit and separate ESC; it gains a one-box whose premium is largely paid by pooling volume with the BEV. One pedal box, one line set and one calibration base across both powertrains. Baseline: the shared platform carries two actuation architectures - the BEV gets an integrated one-box for regen blending, while the 3.0 L MHEV keeps a tandem master cylinder with pneumatic assistance from an electric pump (a throttled petrol six at high load cannot guarantee assistance), plus a separate ESC hydraulic unit. That means two pedal boxes, two bulkhead layouts, two hydraulic line sets, two supplier software stacks and two calibrations for one body. Proposal: fit the same one-box (motor-driven plunger pressure supply, pedal simulator, integrated ESC) to the MHEV too; the 48 V belt starter-generator then gets proper regen blending and the pneumatic chain disappears. Continental MK C1 already integrated actuation, assistance and ESC and cut weight ~30% versus conventional systems; MK C2 weighs 4.7-5 kg and is a further ~20% lighter with fewer components. Mercedes GLC with EQ Technology uses digital brake control with a hydraulic fallback valve. Result: one bulkhead interface, one pedal box, one line routing, one calibration base and one supplier part number at 50,000 units/yr instead of 20,000.

title: Closed-loop air supply with 20-bar reservoir enables fast off-road lift, smaller compressor
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Smaller compressor motor and head, smaller relay/power feed, reduced desiccant and dryer housing; fewer compressor and valve warranty claims from moisture. Lowering no longer wastes energy, so the duty-cycle-driven over-sizing goes away. Baseline: an open air-supply system draws ambient air, compresses it to ~16-18 bar and vents to atmosphere on lowering. To lift a heavy SUV quickly to off-road height (Defender: +75 mm, up to +145 mm total) the compressor is sized for flow, typically a 400-450 W, 12 V unit with high duty-cycle limits, and every lowering throws compressed air away. Proposal: a closed-loop (charged) system - air moves between springs and a 20-bar steel/Al reservoir (6-8 L) with a low-pressure return; lift is mostly reservoir-to-spring transfer (seconds), and the compressor only tops up and pumps back on lowering. Because pressure ratio across the compressor drops (e.g. 8 to 20 bar instead of 1 to 18 bar), a ~250-300 W compressor delivers the required lift energy; air stays dry so dryer desiccant shrinks and condensation-related failures of valves fall. Xiaomi YU7 uses closed dual-chamber air springs; BYD DiSus-A (Denza N9) offers up to 150 mm height travel. For wading, a closed loop also means the intake breathes only on top-up, cutting water-ingestion risk at 900 mm wade.

title: Plug-compatible coil or air corner: steel spring and two-valve damper on volume MHEV
description: [MHEV] On steel-sprung MHEVs the air system (4 air struts, supply unit, reservoir, valve block, lines, 4 height sensors) is replaced by coil springs and two-valve dampers; the common interfaces mean no extra subframe, knuckle or body tooling for the variant. Baseline: air suspension is standard on every trim, so a volume MHEV buyer who never uses off-road height pays for four air springs, compressor, reservoir, valve block, lines and height sensors. Proposal: design the corner so that a steel-spring strut with a two-valve adaptive damper and the air strut share the same top-mount bolt pattern (3x M10 on a 120 mm PCD), the same lower clevis/knuckle interface and the same subframe spring-seat mounting. Steel version: front 54SiCr6 coil (σ ≈ 1,900 MPa design, shot-peened, Zn-phosphate + powder), rear coil on the lower link; dampers with two independent valves (rebound and compression controlled separately) recover much of the comfort band. The Porsche Cayenne (2024 MY) does exactly this - Cayenne, Cayenne S and E-Hybrid have steel springs with two-valve PASM as standard, air optional - and the Audi Q6 e-tron offers steel springs with passive dampers as base and air as an option. Off-road pack, towing pack and all BEVs keep air.

title: Common driven front corner for MHEV and BEV: one knuckle, hub and outboard joint
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] One part number each for knuckle, hub-bearing, outboard CV and caliper carrier at 50,000/yr instead of two at 30,000 and 20,000; avoided second set of forging/casting dies, machining fixtures and validation; fewer service parts. Baseline: on a multi-energy platform the front axle is driven by a transfer-case front differential on the MHEV and by a front e-drive on the BEV. Programmes often let the two front driveshafts, hub-bearing units and knuckles diverge (different spline count, different outboard CV size, different knuckle bore and caliper mount because the BEV is ~400 kg heavier). Proposal: freeze one front corner - knuckle, Gen3 flanged hub-bearing (Ø ~90 mm outer, 33-spline), outboard CV joint size, caliper carrier and wheel-speed sensor - sized for the BEV corner load and the MHEV peak torque, and absorb the differences in the inboard joint and shaft length only. The Range Rover L460 MLA-Flex platform was announced from launch to take a pure-EV version alongside ICE/hybrids, and the shared corner is where that pays most. The heavier BEV load sets bearing size; the MHEV peak front torque (low-range off-road with 3.0 L six and transfer case) sets the outboard joint - in practice both point to the same size class, so the delta in mass is <0.5 kg per corner.

title: Double-wishbone front axle replaces five-link front on shared platform
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Per side two fewer links, two fewer ball joints and four fewer bushes; per car 4 links, 4 ball joints, 8 bushes and ~16 fasteners deleted. Two forged A-arms cost more than single links but less than four. Baseline: premium SUVs often use a five-link front axle (two split lower links, two split upper links, tie-rod) to get a virtual steering axis with low scrub radius and good packaging of large brakes; NIO ES8 Gen 3 and Audi Q6 e-tron both use five-link front suspension. That is 4 links + 1 tie-rod, 4 ball joints at the knuckle and 8 rubber bushes per side. Proposal: a double-wishbone front with a wide-base A-shaped lower arm (forged EN AW-6082-T6, two bushes, one ball joint), an upper A-arm (forged 6082-T6 or Cobapress A356, two bushes, one ball joint) and the tie-rod: 2 arms + tie-rod, 2 ball joints and 4 bushes per side. Xiaomi YU7 uses double-wishbone front with five-link rear. Kingpin offset is controlled by placing the lower ball joint inside the 21-23 in wheel (enabled by a Gen3 hub and a compact radial caliper mount); the larger fixed kingpin axis costs a little steering-feel refinement, which EPS compensation can address.

title: Internal piston-valve CDC damper replaces external side-canister valve
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Removes the side valve housing (machined Al or steel), intermediate tube, port boss weld, O-rings and a leak-test station; outer tube simplifies; air-strut rolling piston no longer needs a canister cut-out. Baseline: many luxury SUV adaptive dampers use a twin-tube body with an EXTERNAL proportional valve - a side canister welded or bolted to the lower section of the reservoir tube, with its own machined valve housing, intermediate tube, O-rings and a laser-welded port boss (ZF notes that on CDC dampers with an external valve, the proportional valve sits externally on the lower section of the damper tube). Proposal: a CDC damper with the proportional solenoid valve INSIDE the piston (or in the base valve) - ZF states CDC works with internal or external valves - wiring routed through a hollow piston rod (Ø20 x 4 mm, 20MnV6 induction-hardened and chrome) to a top connector. This deletes the side canister, its weld boss and the intermediate tube; the outer tube becomes a plain ERW tube (E235/E355). Air-strut packaging benefits too, because the side canister clashes with the air-spring rolling piston and forces offset designs.

title: Single-valve CDC on dual-chamber air trims; two-valve dampers only on steel springs
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Second valve, its coil driver channel in the zone/central controller, and the extra wiring are deleted on four dampers of every air-sprung car; software calibration effort shrinks (two actuators per corner instead of three). Baseline: the platform follows the newest premium practice of fitting two-valve adaptive dampers (separately controlled rebound and compression stages - Porsche Cayenne 2024 MY; Xiaomi YU7 dual-valve CDC) on every trim, including those that also carry switchable-rate air springs. Each two-valve damper carries a second proportional solenoid, a second current-driver channel in the controller and extra wiring. Proposal: fit single-valve CDC where the spring rate is already switchable and keep two-valve only on steel-sprung trims. Reasoning: a switchable-rate air spring already changes body stiffness by typically 30-60%, so the comfort-to-sport band can be widened by the spring, leaving the damper to manage wheel control; independent rebound/compression control earns its cost where the coil rate is fixed. The ride controller then commands two actuators per corner instead of three, which also shrinks calibration effort and test matrices.

title: Dual-chamber switching valve integrated in air-spring rolling piston
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Per corner deletes valve housing/bracket, air line, two fittings and a harness branch; shared moulding of piston and valve seat. Leak paths per corner fall from 4 to 1, lowering warranty. Baseline: a dual-chamber air spring (Porsche Cayenne two-chamber, two-valve; NIO ES8 and Lotus Eletre dual-chamber; Genesis GV90 multi-chamber) often places the additional volume in the strut cap or in a separate can, connected by a short line with an externally mounted solenoid valve, a bracket, two push-in fittings and a dedicated harness branch per corner. Proposal: put the auxiliary volume inside the rolling piston (PA66-GF30 or Al) and mount a 12 V normally-open poppet solenoid (orifice Ø6-8 mm for <50 ms chamber switching) directly in the piston dividing wall, with its connector moulded into the piston/top-mount and routed with the damper CDC lead. No external line, no external valve housing, no extra fittings. The piston volume (typically 0.4-0.7 L) gives a switchable rate change of ~30-50% at design height. Rate switching, the main benefit of the second chamber, is kept unchanged.

title: Powertrain-split disc surface spec: carbide-coated front on MHEV, nitrocarburised on BEV
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] BEV avoids two WC coatings (≈3x base disc cost) and pays only the FNC treatment; MHEV unchanged. Common disc geometry keeps machining and calipers shared. Baseline: to cut brake dust (Euro 7) and avoid rusty discs, the platform fits tungsten-carbide coated front discs on all versions, following Porsche Surface Coated Brake (~0.1 mm WC sprayed at supersonic speed on a galvanised cast-iron disc, up to 90% less dust, standard on Cayenne Turbo and Macan Turbo). Bosch/Buderus iDisc of the same type costs about three times a normal cast-iron disc. Proposal: decide the friction-ring surface by duty cycle. MHEV (regen limited by the 48 V machine, 3,500 kg towing) keeps the WC-coated front disc. The 800V BEV, where e-motors handle ~97% (Cayenne Electric) to 99% (Mercedes claim, GLC EQ) of braking, gets plain GJL-150 high-carbon (3.7-3.9% C) cast-iron discs with gas ferritic nitrocarburising (~570 °C, 2-4 h, 10-20 µm compound layer) for corrosion resistance - a relatively cheap treatment widely used on EV rotors. Dust emission on the BEV is controlled by regen share rather than coating; disc sizes stay common so calipers do not change.

title: Self-locking trapezoidal screw rear-steer actuator replaces ball screw and holding brake
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Rolled trapezoidal screw and polymer/bronze nut replace a ground ball screw with recirculating balls; the holding brake, its driver and connector are deleted. Baseline: a central rear-steer actuator uses a ball screw (efficiency ~90%), which is back-drivable, so it needs a separate electromagnetic holding brake or a spring-centring mechanism to hold the rear wheels straight under lateral tyre forces when unpowered or faulted. Proposal: for a reduced rear-steer angle of ±4.5-5 deg (GLC EQ 4.5 deg, Cayenne Electric 5 deg, vs Range Rover L460 7.3 deg) use a rolled trapezoidal (ACME-type, Tr 20x4) screw in 42CrMo4 QT with a bronze-filled PA or CuSn12 nut. With a lead angle below ~4 deg and friction 0.1-0.15, the screw is self-locking: lateral tyre loads cannot back-drive it, so the holding brake and its control can be deleted. Lower efficiency (~35-45%) needs more motor torque, but the shorter stroke at 5 deg and the slower slew rate demanded by rear steer (typically <40 deg/s at the road wheel) keep peak power within a standard 12 V BLDC (≈300-400 W). Thread rolling replaces ball-track grinding.

title: Constant-ratio steering rack when rear-wheel steering is fitted
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Broached constant-pitch teeth replace forged/special-profile variable teeth; simpler pinion and gauging; tooling and quality inspection cost fall. The steering function is preserved by software on the RWS already paid for. Baseline: the front steering gear uses a variable-ratio rack (e.g. 15:1 on centre falling to ~11:1 at lock) to reduce turns lock-to-lock on a large SUV; the variable tooth profile is produced by warm/cold forging or special broaching of the rack teeth plus precise mating pinion, with dedicated gauges. When rear-wheel steering is standard (Range Rover L460: all versions, up to 7.3 deg; turning circle under 11 m) the RWS already shortens the effective wheelbase at low speed and supplies the parking-speed agility the variable rack was bought for. Proposal: on RWS-equipped vehicles fit a constant-ratio rack (~13.5:1) with conventional broached teeth on a C45/ 42CrMo4 induction-hardened rack bar, and use the RWS out-of-phase gain map plus EPS assist to tune low-speed effort and turns lock-to-lock. Variable-ratio racks are retained only if a non-RWS variant exists.

title: EPS active kickback damping deletes off-road steering damper
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes the steering damper, brackets and fasteners on the off-road pack; the function is delivered by EPS calibration on hardware that already exists. Baseline: off-road-focused SUVs often add a hydraulic steering damper (tie-rod mounted, ~1.2 kg, twin-tube, Ø30 mm) to stop rock and rut kickback reaching the driver, or rely on hydraulic power steering for natural damping. Toyota states that on the Land Cruiser 250, the first Land Cruiser with electric power steering, EPS reduces kickback during off-road driving. Proposal: make kickback rejection an EPS function - the column/rack torque sensor and motor-position signal detect high-frequency rack-force spikes (>8-10 Hz) and the motor applies counter-torque within ~5 ms; an off-road terrain mode raises the active damping gain and sets an end-of-travel soft stop. The hardware steering damper, its two brackets, ball-joint mount and fasteners are deleted on the off-road pack. The rack-parallel EPS motor is checked for peak current at kickback events (≈80-100 A on 12 V for <100 ms), usually within the existing power stage.

title: Extruded 6082 rails with cast nodes for length-variant rear subframe
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Replaces several large casting dies with four node dies and a few extrusion dies; variants become cut-length changes. Extrusions are cheaper per kg than structural casting and do not need heat treatment of the full part. Baseline: an all-aluminium luxury SUV (NIO ES8 Gen 3 claims 96.4% aluminium body and chassis; Lotus Eletre aluminium multi-link front and rear) typically uses a large one-piece cast aluminium rear subframe. Every track width, wheelbase-related mount change, or MHEV vs BEV mount pattern (rear differential vs rear e-drive) needs a new die (€1.5-2.5M each) and the casting carries all the mass. Proposal: a hybrid subframe - two longitudinal and two transverse EN AW-6082-T6 extrusions (multi-cell profiles, 3-4 mm walls) joined to four low-pressure cast AlSi7Mg0.3-T6 corner nodes that carry the link pick-ups and body mounts, joined by MIG welding (or FSW on straight seams) and solution-free T6 nodes. Track and powertrain-mount differences are absorbed by cutting extrusions to length and by two bolt-on powertrain brackets (rear diff or e-drive), so one node set and one profile set cover MHEV, BEV and two track widths. Extrusion dies cost €20-60k each.

title: Hydraulic rebound stop in damper replaces rebound spring and off-road travel limiter
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes the rebound spring, its seat and guide, the external travel limiter and its brackets; the HRS adds a sleeve and secondary piston. End-of-travel bellows damage and clunk warranty decline. Baseline: long-travel off-road air suspension (Land Rover Defender: +75 mm off-road height, up to +145 mm total lift and 500 mm articulation) must stop the wheel at full droop without the bellows over-extending and without a metallic clunk. Typical hardware is an internal steel rebound spring (or polyurethane rebound buffer) inside the damper, plus an external travel-limiting element or a reinforced bellows end stop, each tuned for the extra droop of the off-road height. Proposal: a hydraulic rebound stop (HRS) inside the damper - in the last 25-35 mm of extension a secondary piston enters a tapered sleeve in the pressure tube and builds damping force progressively (up to ~15-20 kN) so the wheel decelerates without a spring or strap; the steel rebound spring and the external limiter are deleted, and the air spring is protected because velocity is near zero at end of travel. At the off-road height the HRS engagement is reached only in deep droop (articulation) cases, where its progressive force also reduces wheel lift. Same damper body for MHEV and BEV; the HRS sleeve length is the only tuning variable.

title: Air-supply intake ducted into wade-safe body cavity deletes remote intake line and filter
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Long intake hose, remote intake filter, 8-10 clips and a grommet deleted; short spigot and breather added. Fewer intake-related water-ingress warranty claims on compressors. Baseline: to keep water out of the compressor at deep wading (Defender: 900 mm, with a Wade programme that raises ride height), the air-supply unit low on the underbody or in the spare-wheel well has an extended intake hose (PA12, 2-3 m) routed up to a high point in a pillar or wing, with its own intake filter, clip set and drain. Proposal: mount the air-supply unit (or only its intake) so that it breathes from an existing sealed, high body cavity - e.g. the rear quarter/D-pillar cavity behind the trim, already above the 900 mm wade line - via a short moulded spigot with a sintered PE breather and the cavity itself as the settling volume; combine with the closed-loop supply (which inhales rarely) to remove the remote filter. Polestar/EV9-type BEVs have a lot of free volume at the rear quarter, and on the MHEV the same cavity exists.

title: One 48 V BLDC motor family shared by active-roll and rear-steer actuators
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Lamination, magnet, sensor and inverter volumes triple on one design (2 eARC + 1 RWS motors per car); one stamping die and one inverter PCB; RWS harness gauge falls (≈4 mm² → 1.5 mm²). Baseline: a luxury SUV with both 48 V active roll control (Range Rover L460: 1,400 Nm, 900 Nm within 200 ms) and rear-wheel steering, as Range Rover L460 and Lotus Eletre have, buys two unrelated motor designs from two actuator suppliers: a high-torque 48 V BLDC for each eARC actuator and a 12 V BLDC in the RWS actuator, each with its own stator lamination, magnet grade, rotor-position sensor and inverter. Proposal: specify one 48 V outer-diameter Ø80 mm BLDC family (same lamination M270-35A, same NdFeB grade, same resolver/ TMR position sensor, same 3-phase GaN/MOSFET inverter board) with two stack lengths: long for eARC, short for RWS. The RWS moves to 48 V, which also halves current for the same power (≈8 A instead of 16 A at 400 W), shrinking the harness. On the MHEV the 48 V comes from the MHEV battery; on the BEV from the 800 V→48 V DC/DC already sized for eARC.

title: Solid nitrocarburised rear disc for BEV replaces vented zinc-flake disc
description: [800V BEV] Solid disc uses ~2 kg less iron per disc and a simpler core-less mould (no vane core); Zn-flake coating deleted; corrosion-related disc/pad replacements under warranty fall. Baseline: large BEV SUVs carry big ventilated rear discs (Audi Q6 e-tron: 350 mm cast iron; Kia EV9: 345/360 mm ventilated) with a Zn-flake coated hat and a bare friction ring that rusts because regen does almost all braking - VW chose rear drums on the ID.4 precisely because rear discs are used so rarely they corrode. Proposal: a SOLID 350 x 20 mm rear disc in GJL-150 high-carbon grey iron (vs vented 350 x 28 mm), fully ferritic-nitrocarburised (gas FNC ~570 °C, 2-4 h, 10-20 µm epsilon layer + diffusion zone) which protects both hat and friction ring and replaces the Zn-flake coating. FNC is a relatively cheap corrosion treatment; most EV brake systems use nitrocarburised rear rotors, and GM reported ~70% fewer brake warranty claims after introducing FNC. Thermal check: at 97-99% regen share the rear disc sees a few full-friction stops per year; a single 100-0 km/h stop of a 2,800 kg SUV with 30% rear bias puts ~0.32 MJ into two rear discs, a ~45 K rise in a 6.5 kg solid disc - acceptable. Emergency repeated-stop cases are re-verified.

title: Cast-forged (Cobapress) A356 front knuckle replaces forged 6082-T6 knuckle
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Cheaper input (secondary-grade A356 ingot vs 6082 extruded bar), one forging stroke instead of three, near-net shape cuts flash and machining time; recycled-content A356 lowers metal cost. Baseline: luxury SUV front knuckles are commonly hot-forged EN AW-6082-T6 from extruded bar: multi-stage forging (bust, block, finish), trimming, solution + age, then heavy 5-axis machining; forging flash and bar cut waste put the buy-to-fly ratio near 1.8-2.0. Proposal: Cobapress cast-forge process - a near-net A356 (AlSi7Mg0.3) preform cast in a permanent mould, then forged in ONE press stroke while warm, then T6. Saint Jean Industries states the single stroke closes internal casting defects, gives a fatigue-resistant skin and suits knuckles, wheel carriers and control arms; >100 million parts have been produced, and their Peugeot 406 Coupé hub carrier weighed 3.2 kg with 50% less mass and 30% more stiffness than steel. Expect UTS ~310-330 MPa, elongation 8-10% (forged 6082-T6: 310-340 MPa, 10-12%), so the knuckle grows ~5-8% in section/mass, but buy weight falls to ~1.2x finished and machining stock is smaller because the preform carries cored features.

title: Cold-headed 38B3 boron ball studs replace turned 42CrMo4 studs in link joints
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Wire at lower alloy cost than CrMo bar; near-zero chip loss (material yield ~95% vs ~60% turned); header runs at 60-100 parts/min versus ~1 min/part turning; thread rolling replaces cutting. Baseline: ball joints on the front links and rear toe/camber links use ball studs turned from 42CrMo4 QT bar, with the ball ground and the taper and thread machined - typically 10-14 joints per car on a multi-link SUV (NIO ES8 Gen 3 uses five-link suspension front and rear). Proposal: ball studs cold-headed (multi-stage, 5-station header) from 38B3 / 32CrB4 boron wire, thread rolled, then through-hardened and tempered to 10.9-equivalent (1,040-1,200 MPa UTS) and induction-hardened only on the ball (58-62 HRC), with the ball finished by centreless grinding. Cold heading gives continuous grain flow round the ball-to-neck fillet, raising fatigue strength ~10-15% over a turned stud of the same section, so neck diameter can be kept. Boron steel hardens through at a lower alloy cost than CrMo.

title: Bonded-to-bar stabiliser bushes delete axial retaining collars
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Four collars and a crimping press operation deleted per car; grease/liner deleted; squeak warranty eliminated. Bonding is done in-line at the bar supplier. Baseline: passive stabiliser bars (and the bar halves of active-roll actuators) are held laterally by slip-fit rubber bushes in clamp brackets, with crimped or swaged steel/aluminium collars either side of each bush to stop the bar migrating sideways, plus a PTFE liner or grease to avoid stick-slip squeak. Proposal: vulcanise or post-bond (two-part primer/adhesive system, curing in the e-coat oven or induction cured at ~160 °C) the natural-rubber bush directly to the bar, so the bush twists in shear instead of slipping. The bond provides lateral location, so the 4 collars and their crimping operation are deleted, and squeak from slip is gone. Shear strain at ±15° bar twist on a Ø42 mm bush with 10 mm wall is within ~±60%, acceptable for NR 55-60 ShA. The concept matters more now because BEV volume trims and Polestar 3-style chassis rely on passive bars rather than active roll, and bush/top-mount refinements were part of Rivian’s Gen-2 R1S secondary-ride fix.

title: Sliced 6082 extrusion-profile rear camber links replace forged aluminium links
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Saw-slicing a press-quenched profile replaces bar-cut multi-stage forging and separate heat treatment; die cost drops by ~80%, and buy-to-fly improves because there is no flash. Baseline: aluminium multi-link rear axles (NIO ES8 Gen 3 five-link front and rear in a 96.4% aluminium body and chassis; Lotus Eletre aluminium multi-link front and rear) use forged EN AW-6082-T6 for most links, including lightly loaded camber and toe links: bar cut, 2-3 forging stages, trimming, heat-treat, machining. Proposal: for the planar, lightly loaded rear camber links, extrude a closed-section EN AW-6082 profile whose cross-section IS the link plan-form (I/double-I web with the two bush eyes as integral hollows, length direction = extrusion thickness), then saw slices of 30-40 mm thickness, CNC-machine the eye bores and chamfers, and age to T6 (press-quenched profile). Sawing a slice takes seconds and the die costs €20-40k vs €150-250k for a forging die set. Profile walls of 4-6 mm give a buckling load comfortably above the camber-link design load (typically 10-15 kN compression) for a 300-350 mm link; the extruded grain runs across the slice, so fatigue is checked against the transverse properties (~10% lower than longitudinal).

title: PA12-coated Zn-Al steel brake pipes replace copper-nickel pipe runs
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Coated steel tube costs ~40-55% of CuNi per metre; copper price volatility removed from the BOM. Pre-bent line modules also reduce in-plant routing time and the one-box layout shortens total pipe length. Baseline: premium vehicles frequently use copper-nickel (CuNi10Fe1Mn) 4.75 mm brake pipe for its corrosion resistance and easy bending - typically 10-12 m per SUV from the one-box/ESC unit to four corners and the flex hoses. Proposal: double-wall brazed low-carbon steel tube (DIN 74234 / SAE J527 type) with a Zn-Al (Galfan-type) metallic layer plus extruded PA12 or PA11 overcoat (~150-200 µm) giving >1,000 h neutral salt spray and stone-chip resistance; use CuNi only for the two short highly-flexed runs near the corners if packaging demands. Bending and flaring tools are the same family (4.75 mm). With a one-box (Continental MK C2-class units weigh 4.7-5 kg and integrate booster and ESC) there is one hydraulic block, so the line set is short and fully pre-bent off-line as a harness-like module.

title: Extruded 6060 tube air reservoir with spun ends replaces welded steel tank
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Deletes welding of shells, bosses and brackets, the leak-test rework loop and painting; integral rails replace two welded brackets; ~2 kg lighter. Natural corrosion resistance of aluminium removes paint. Baseline: air-suspension reservoirs are often two deep-drawn DC04/S355 steel half-shells or a rolled tube with welded domed ends, welded bosses for fittings and mounting brackets, then e-coated and painted; a 6-8 L, 20 bar tank weighs ~4-5 kg. Closed-loop dual-chamber systems such as the Xiaomi YU7 rely on a reservoir as part of the air circuit. Proposal: an EN AW-6060-T6 (or 6082-T6 for higher pressure) extruded tube Ø120 x 3.5 mm with integral extruded mounting rails, ends closed by hot spinning (CNC flow-spinning at ~400 °C into a hemispherical dome, ~20 s/end), a machined port boss in one spun end and an O-ring plug fitting. No welds, no paint (natural oxide or conversion coat), mounting through the extruded rails with two isolators. Hoop stress at 20 bar = p·r/t = 2.0 MPa x 60 / 3.5 ≈ 34 MPa, well under 6060-T6 yield (~150 MPa) with burst margin >3.

title: Moulded PA6-GF30 air-spring guide sleeve replaces aluminium outer guide tube
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Moulded sleeve replaces drawn and coated aluminium tube and crimp rings; integrates dust-boot location; mass saving reduces unsprung mass slightly. No coating line needed. Baseline: guided (sleeve-type) air springs on luxury SUVs - needed for the thin, comfortable bellows used in dual-chamber springs such as those on Porsche Cayenne, NIO ES8 and Lotus Eletre - carry an outer guide tube that limits bellows diameter growth under 8-12 bar: usually an aluminium EN AW-6060 drawn tube, crimped at both ends, with a protective coating, ~0.5-0.7 kg per spring. Proposal: injection-moulded PA6-GF30 (heat-stabilised, impact-modified) guide sleeve with circumferential ribs (wall 2.5 mm, rib 1.5 mm) and moulded snap features replacing the end crimp, plus an integrated dust-boot lip. Hoop load from the bellows on the sleeve is modest because the cord layers carry most pressure; e.g. a bellows bulging against the sleeve at 10 bar on a Ø90 mm sleeve gives ~p·r/t = 1 x 45 / 2.5 ≈ 18 MPa, inside PA6-GF30 long-term allowable (~25-30 MPa conditioned at 80 °C). The moulded sleeve is lighter (~0.25 kg) and cheaper.

title: Hollow 20MnV6 damper rod with friction-welded end replaces solid chromed rod
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Less steel per rod and less turning (end piece only); bore is free cable channel avoiding drilling a solid rod; if nitrocarburised, chrome plating and its effluent treatment costs are removed. Baseline: adaptive damper rods on luxury SUVs are solid 20MnV6 or C45 bar, Ø20-22 mm, induction-hardened and hard-chromed, with the piston end and top thread turned from the same bar; a front rod weighs ~1.0-1.2 kg. Two-valve dampers (Cayenne 2024 MY) and dual-valve CDC (Xiaomi YU7) also need a cable route for the valves. Proposal: a cold-drawn welded-and-drawn E355 / 20MnV6 tube Ø22 x 4.5 mm for the sliding section, rotary-friction-welded to a solid turned end piece (thread and piston seat), then induction-hardened and chrome-plated (or nitrocarburised + oxidised to delete Cr(VI) chrome). Bending stiffness of a Ø22x4.5 tube is ~88% of a Ø22 solid rod (I ratio = 1 − (13/22)^4 ≈ 0.88), so buckling and side-load margins change little, mass falls ~40%, and the bore doubles as the wiring channel for in-piston valves.

title: Cast-in rear-steer actuator mounting pads on rear subframe delete bolted brackets
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Deletes two actuator brackets, four bolts and two inserts; machining of pads done in the existing subframe set-up; better geometry reduces rear toe adjustment time at alignment. Baseline: where rear-wheel steering is optional, the rear subframe is designed without it and the central RWS actuator is attached through two bolted cast or stamped brackets (plus four extra bolts and two weld nuts/inserts), while non-RWS cars use a fixed toe-link bracket set. With RWS standard (Range Rover L460: all versions; Lotus Eletre: active rear steer), the bracket set is pure overhead. Proposal: cast the four actuator mounting pads (M12, machined faces ±0.1 mm, positioned by the same CNC set-up as the link pick-ups) directly into the aluminium rear subframe node (AlSi7Mg0.3-T6 LPDC or AlSi10MnMg HPDC), and machine them in the same clamping as the toe-link pick-ups so actuator-to-link geometry is tighter (toe tolerance improves from ~±10 to ±5 arc-min before alignment). If a non-RWS variant must remain, it uses a fixed toe-link bar bolted to the same pads.

ideaData.dfmDfa: Per EDU: ~25-35 fewer parts (gear pair, synchro/dog ring, fork, actuator, sensor, bearings, seals). No shift-fork adjustment at assembly, no position-sensor teach-in. Serviceability improves: no shift actuator to replace after water ingress.

title: Single dog-locker cartridge fits both MHEV hypoid rear axle and BEV rear EDU
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] One development, one PPAP, one actuator/sensor family and one software function; volume aggregation from ~15,000 off-road-pack MHEV + ~10,000 BEV lockers into one 25,000/yr part gives ~12-15% piece-price leverage plus avoided duplicate tooling (~€1.2M). Baseline: a two-powertrain platform typically sources two different rear locking devices — a dog-type or ball-ramp unit inside the MHEV hypoid rear axle (ring gear ~215-225 mm) and a separate locking unit inside the single-motor BEV rear EDU, each with its own actuator, sensor, software and supplier PPAP. Proposal: specify one electro-mechanical dog-locker cartridge — case, side gears, 16MnCr5 dog ring, axial electromagnet coil (12 V, 3 A hold) and engagement detection — sized to the governing torque case and fitted into both carriers via a common spigot and 8 × M10 bolt circle. Ring gear and carrier flanges stay powertrain-specific; the cartridge is identical. The Defender offers an Active Locking Rear Differential and the Ineos Grenadier electronically actuated lockers; both are single-powertrain designs. Torque check: MHEV rear axle in low range sees 3.0 L I6 ~550 Nm × 1st 4.7 × low 2.6 × final 3.7 × 0.6 rear share ≈ 14.9 kNm — this governs; the BEV single rear motor sees ~350 Nm × 10.5 = 3.7 kNm, so the cartridge is oversized for BEV but avoids a second development, PPAP and spares chain.

title: Standard-duty ESC unit on BEV: motor torque handles crawl and descent braking
description: [800V BEV] [Off-road] Heavy-duty ESC variant (premium ~€35-€55) and uprated rear brake package (~€20-€30) deleted on BEV; one fewer ESC part number reduces calibration and supplier variant cost; brake wear in off-road use falls. Baseline: off-road SUVs run off-road cruise and hill-descent with the brake system: Ford's Trail Control manages throttle and brakes to hold a set speed up and down grades. Sustained hydraulic modulation on long descents forces a heavy-duty ESC variant — larger pump motor (~350-450 W), bigger low-pressure accumulators, uprated valve coils, thermal model — plus rear brake cooling margin. Proposal: on the BEV, crawl and descent control are done primarily by the motors: each motor holds speed down to ~0.5 km/h in 4-quadrant torque control (Rivian Gen 2 Quad adjusts torque independently at each wheel), and regenerative torque of ~250-350 Nm per motor × 10.5:1 reduction gives 2.6-3.7 kNm per wheel-pair — enough to hold a 2.9 t SUV on a 40% descent (required ≈ 2,900 × 9.81 × sin 21.8° × 0.40 m ≈ 4.2 kNm total, shared by two axles). Friction brakes only act per-wheel for cross-axle slip and at standstill. The ESC hydraulic unit can then be the standard-duty unit shared with non-off-road trims; the pump duty cycle in descents falls by ~80-90%. MHEV keeps the heavy-duty unit.

title: 48 V torque fill allows shorter 2.0:1 low range and lighter planetary on MHEV
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] Smaller, lighter planetary (gear steel, machining and heat-treat volume −20-25%), one planet and its needle bearing fewer, lighter carrier; the 48 V hardware is already on the vehicle, so only calibration is added. Baseline: luxury MHEV off-roaders use a two-speed transfer case with a ~2.5-2.7:1 low range (planetary, 20MnCr5 sun/planets, ring gear), sized so that at engine idle the vehicle crawls at ~2-3 km/h without stalling and can restart on steep grades with a trailer. Proposal: exploit the 48 V motor-generator already on the engine (as Toyota did when adding 48 V to the Land Cruiser 250 with its eight-speed automatic and low range) to fill torque at 700-1,200 rpm: a P0 belt starter-generator of ~50-60 Nm at the motor and ~2.7:1 pulley ratio adds ~135-160 Nm at the crank, raising effective low-speed crank torque from ~350-400 Nm to ~500-550 Nm. Required wheel torque for a 45% grade start at 2.9 t is unchanged, so the low-range ratio can fall from 2.6:1 to ~2.0:1 for the same wheel torque. Benefits: planetary with 3 instead of 4 planets, ~25% narrower face width, smaller ring gear OD, lower carrier torque (the transmitted low-range torque falls ~23%), and a crawl speed at idle of ~3-3.5 km/h controlled by torque-converter slip and Trail-style speed control. Transfer-case housing and chain stay common.

title: Passive bars with 12 V centre-split clutch replace 48 V roll actuators off-road
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Swaps two high-power 48 V actuators, power electronics and harness for passive bars plus one low-power 12 V dog-clutch actuator; also removes 48 V load (~2-3 kW peak) from the DC/DC budget on the BEV and from the 48 V battery on the MHEV. Baseline: luxury SUVs in this class get both on-road body control and off-road articulation from 48 V electromechanical roll-control units front and rear: two ~1.5-2.5 kW motor-gear actuators, a 48 V supply branch, ECU and roll-rate sensing. Proposal: on the off-road trim, fit conventional tubular bars (front Ø28 × 4 mm 34MnB5 quenched tube, rear Ø22 solid 52CrMoV4) and split only the front bar with a 12 V motor-driven dog clutch at its centre; it re-couples automatically above ~30 km/h. Toyota introduced exactly this Stabilizer with Disconnection Mechanism (SDM) on the Land Cruiser 250 — its first Land Cruiser with EPS and SDM — and Lexus uses E-KDSS on the GX 550 Overtrail. Articulation: front wheel travel rises ~20-30% with the bar split, delivering most of the off-road RTI benefit of a 48 V system; on-road roll gradient stays ~3.5-4.0°/g with passive bars plus the air springs. The 48 V pair (~€650-€850) becomes passive bars plus one 12 V splitter (~€260-€280 all-in).

title: Membrane-vented sealed EDUs and pack reach 900 mm wading without raised breather lines
description: [800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes ~4-6 m of PA12 breather tubing, a breather manifold, 12-18 clips, grommets through body panels and the body-side bracket; replaces them with three €2-€4 membrane vents. Also removes a warranty source (kinked or disconnected breather hoses causing water ingress). Baseline: to meet 850-900 mm wading, many BEV SUV programmes inherit ICE practice — breather hoses from each EDU gearbox and from the pack pressure-relief valve routed up to a high point in the body (C-pillar or wheel-arch top), with clips, a manifold and long PA12 lines. Proposal: no raised breather lines on the BEV. Each EDU gets a screw-in ePTFE membrane vent (IP68/IP69K, 1.0 bar water-entry pressure ≥ 10 m head, airflow ~2 l/min @ 70 mbar) mounted directly on the housing, behind a labyrinth splash shield; the pack keeps its burst disc and uses a two-stage vent (ePTFE membrane for breathing + spring valve for thermal-event venting). With 900 mm water the hydrostatic head at the lowest vent is ~0.06 bar — an order of magnitude below the membrane entry pressure. Sudden cooling (hot EDU at 90 °C entering 10 °C water) creates up to ~150-200 mbar internal vacuum, so the vent is sized to equalise in <60 s and the seal lips are spec-rated for 0.3 bar. Mercedes says the G 580 battery sits in a sealed torsion-resistant housing and fords 850 mm; GWM rates the Tank 500 Hi4-T battery IP67 for 30 min

title: Dog-type rear e-locker plus brake vectoring replaces multi-plate active rear differential
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] Deletes the plate pack, apply piston/ball-ramp, modulating actuator motor or pump, oil cooler/pump and temperature model; the dog locker costs roughly a third of an active clutch differential. Baseline: many luxury MHEV SUVs fit an active rear differential with a multi-plate wet clutch between the case and one side gear (8-12 plates, ball-ramp or hydraulic actuation, electric motor or pump, temperature model) to give both on-road yaw tuning and off-road lock-up. Proposal: on the off-road MHEV, replace it with a dog-type electronic locker (on/off, solenoid-actuated dog ring) inside a conventional open bevel differential, and deliver on-road yaw assistance by brake-based torque vectoring in the ESC (inside-rear brake pulses of 5-15 bar in corner exit). Toyota fits exactly this hardware to the Land Cruiser 250 — automatic limited-slip by brakes on the base grade, rear e-locker on upper grades — and Lexus a locking rear differential on the GX 550 Overtrail. Physics: a locked dog gives 100% lock torque at zero slip, more than a plate pack (limited by plate area and heat: ~1,500-2,500 Nm and minutes before thermal cut-out under sand/mud slip); on-road, brake vectoring achieves ~70-80% of the yaw moment of an active diff at low lateral g, which is the luxury SUV use envelope.

title: Rear EDU heat dumped into battery loop at crawl instead of upsizing front radiator
description: [800V BEV] [Off-road] Avoids LT radiator upsizing (core, larger fan or second fan stage, shroud) for the off-road/tow derivative; one 4-port valve and software are added, reusing the chiller capacity already paid for by fast charging. Baseline: BEV off-roaders sized for low-speed high-load (crawl in low range, trailer at 5-10 km/h, 40 °C ambient) reject EDU losses through the front low-temperature radiator, which must be upsized (core +25-35% face area, second fan stage) because ram air is near zero; the battery loop, meanwhile, is sized for fast charging (~25-35 kW chiller) and sits mostly idle at crawl. Proposal: add a 4-port coolant valve linking the rear EDU oil-to-water heat exchanger to the battery loop at crawl speeds (<20 km/h, off-road or tow mode). A 100-115 kWh pack has ~250-300 kJ/K thermal mass (cells ~0.95-1.1 kJ/kg·K × ~600 kg cells); absorbing ~4-6 kW of EDU loss for a 30-minute crawl would alone raise pack temperature by ~25-35 K (5 kW × 1,800 s = 9 MJ ÷ ~275 kJ/K ≈ 33 K), so the strategy caps pack inlet at 40 °C and runs the chiller (idle at crawl) to move the heat into the refrigerant circuit and its condenser fan; the pack mass buffers transients only. Net: the LT radiator stays at road-car size. Rivian made its Gen 2 Quad motors oil-cooled to improve thermal management for low-speed off-road driving; Mercedes cools G 580 cells via three cooling levels — sho

title: Single high-mounted vent manifold for MHEV gearbox, transfer case and both axles
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] Tube length −35-45%, clips −50%, three vent caps and two body grommets deleted; one manifold replaces four separate high-point brackets. Fewer routing paths also remove a recurrent warranty cause (pinched breather → seal blow-out → water ingress). Baseline: an MHEV off-roader rated for 900 mm wading (Defender, Range Rover L460) must vent the 8-speed automatic, the two-speed transfer case and the front and rear differentials above the water line. Typical practice is four independent breather hoses, each with its own route up the bulkhead/body, its own vent cap and separate clips — ~10-12 m of tube in total and four routing paths with interference risk. Proposal: route each unit's short breather (PA12, 6 × 1 mm) to a single blow-moulded HDPE vent manifold (4-into-1 with internal baffles and a drain-back slope of 5°) mounted behind the front bumper at ~950 mm above ground on the wing-to-radiator support; one ePTFE membrane cap vents to atmosphere. Volumes are small (each unit breathes <0.5 l per thermal cycle) so one 8 mm outlet is adequate. Rear axle line runs along the existing fuel/brake line clip-path, removing three separate body penetrations. Toyota highlights that the 48V Land Cruiser keeps its 700 mm wading by positioning hybrid components high — the same "keep the vent high, keep it short" logic.

ideaData.title: Single high-mounted vent manifold for MHEV gearbox, transfer case and both axles
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: an MHEV off-roader rated for 900 mm wading (Defender, Range Rover L460) must vent the 8-speed automatic, the two-speed transfer case and the front and rear differentials above the water line. Typical practice is four independent breather hoses, each with its own route up the bulkhead/body, its own vent cap and separate clips — ~10-12 m of tube in total and four routing paths with interference risk. Proposal: route each unit's short breather (PA12, 6 × 1 mm) to a single blow-moulded HDPE vent manifold (4-into-1 with internal baffles and a drain-back slope of 5°) mounted behind the front bumper at ~950 mm above ground on the wing-to-radiator support; one ePTFE membrane cap vents to atmosphere. Volumes are small (each unit breathes <0.5 l per thermal cycle) so one 8 mm outlet is adequate. Rear axle line runs along the existing fuel/brake line clip-path, removing three separate body penetrations. Toyota highlights that the 48V Land Cruiser keeps its 700 mm wading by positioning hybrid components high — the same "keep the vent high, keep it short" logic.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Tube length −35-45%, clips −50%, three vent caps and two body grommets deleted; one manifold replaces four separate high-point brackets. Fewer routing paths also remove a recurrent warranty cause (pinched breather → seal blow-out → water ingress).
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Trim-line routing time −2 to −3 min; manifold is a single blow-moulded part (one tool ~€40k). Lines can be pre-assembled to the manifold as a harness-style kit delivered in sequence.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Kit with colour-coded quick connectors (VDA QC 8 mm) keyed per unit; one mounting point with two M6 bolts; part count −18 to −24. Service: single inspection point for all breathers.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Low-Medium — content and labour reduction with warranty upside
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Per MHEV: tube €4 + 3 caps €4.5 + clips/grommets €3 + labour 2.5 min × €0.8 = €2 → €13.5, minus manifold €4 and connectors €2 = €7.5, plus warranty avoidance €4-€11 = €11.5-€18.5 per MHEV × MHEV share 50-55% of 50,000 → €6-€10 per vehicle (fleet average). Range €6-€10 per vehicle (fleet average) × 50,000 vehicles/yr = €0.30M-€0.50M/yr.

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: cross-communication of oil mist between units (ATF into axle). Validate with internal baffles and check-valve per inlet; wade test 900 mm with hot driveline into cold water (thermal shock), ISO 16750-4; inspect for oil migration after 100 h dyno.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Inspired by / benchmarked against: Toyota Land Cruiser 250 Hybrid 48V (2025) / Land Rover Defender (2020-) — LC250 48V keeps 700 mm wading by positioning the motor-generator high; Defender rated to 900 mm wading. How this differs: We apply the same high-placement principle to all driveline breathers by merging them into one manifold

title: Brake-based trail-turn assist meets off-road turning target without rear-axle steer
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Achieves the off-road turning target in software using the existing ESC hydraulic unit, avoiding RWS hardware on off-road-only buyers who do not want the RWS option. Baseline: luxury SUVs reach tight-trail turning circles by specifying rear-axle steering (±5-7°, electromechanical actuator ~€500-€700) or, on quad-motor BEVs, by motor counter-rotation (Rivian Kick Turn, G 580 G-Steering). Proposal: on off-road trims that do not take RWS, fit a brake-based trail-turn function: at <20 km/h, >270° handwheel angle and low range/off-road mode, ESC applies 20-40 bar to the inside rear brake while the front axle drives, pivoting the vehicle about the inside rear wheel. Ford's Trail Turn Assist on Bronco does exactly this, braking the inside rear wheel to tighten the radius. Expected effect on a 3.0 m wheelbase SUV on gravel: turning circle 12.4 m → ~10.6-11.0 m (−12-15%), close to the ~11.0 m achieved by 5° RWS. On the dual-motor BEV the rear EDU torque is reduced and the front motor drives, so regen recovers some energy. Rivian blocks Kick Turn on high-friction surfaces using friction estimation — we use the same estimator to inhibit trail-turn on tarmac to protect tyres and driveline.

title: Detachable coded towball replaces electrically deployable towbar for 3,500 kg towing
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] Deletes the deploy motor, gearbox, pawl, two position sensors, ECU/LIN node, switch and harness; a mechanical receiver and a reed switch remain. Also removes a recurrent warranty item (deploy motor corrosion from road salt). Baseline: luxury SUVs rated to 3,500 kg (Defender 110: 3,500 kg with up to 150 kg nose weight) increasingly fit an electrically deployable tow bar — a motor, worm gear, locking pawl, position sensors, ECU and switch that swing a fixed ball under the bumper. Proposal: on the MHEV (the 3,500 kg tow variant; Range Rover Electric, for comparison, is rated 2,500 kg), fit a detachable towball that plugs into a hidden receiver in the rear crash-management carrier: 42CrMo4+QT ball neck (Rm ≥ 900 MPa) with a ball-lock spigot (four 12 mm hardened balls), locking indicator (green/red) and key. A passive reed-switch in the receiver tells the body controller that the ball is fitted, enabling trailer-stability and parking-sensor muting — the same function the electric unit provides. The carrier, cross-member and 13-pin socket mount are unchanged, so D-value (~18 kN for 3,500 kg trailer / 3,250 kg vehicle) and S-value (150 kg) certification carries over to ECE R55.

title: One 850 W 48 V fan replaces twin 12 V fans for crawl/tow cooling
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] One motor and controller instead of two; 12 V heavy-gauge cable and second fuse deleted; shroud simpler (one opening). 48 V electronics benefit from lower current (smaller MOSFETs and connector). Baseline: a 3.0 L I6 MHEV specified for 3,500 kg towing and low-range crawl at 40 °C ambient needs ~25-30 kW heat rejection at near-zero ram air. Typical solution: twin 12 V brushless fans (2 × 600 W) in a two-motor shroud, fed by a 12 V high-current circuit (2 × 50 A fuses, heavy cables from the battery) — expensive on the 12 V side because current at full load is ~100 A. Proposal: since the MHEV already has a 48 V bus (belt or integrated starter-generator and 48 V Li-ion pack), fit one 850 W 48 V brushless fan (Ø 500 mm, 9 blades, PA66-GF30 shroud with flap louvres for ram-air bypass). Current at 48 V is ~18 A, so the cable drops from 16 mm² to 4 mm² and one fuse. Air flow: one Ø500 mm fan at 850 W ≈ 4,200-4,600 m³/h at 250 Pa — comparable to two Ø400 mm 600 W fans in this core size. Off-road crawl and trailer duty are the sizing cases; road driving is ram-air dominated. Land Cruiser 250 48 V shows Toyota fitting 48 V hardware to an off-roader without compromising its capabilities.

title: Range-shift without synchroniser: dog shift at standstill with output speed matching
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] Removes the synchroniser ring, blocker and strut keys, the friction-cone machining on the gear, and allows a smaller, slower actuator (lower force spec); simplifies calibration. Baseline: luxury two-speed transfer cases (Defender twin-speed, Range Rover) allow high/low shifting on the move up to ~60 km/h, which requires a synchroniser (brass/carbon cone ring, blocker, strut keys) on the range sleeve plus a fast, high-force actuator. Proposal: delete the synchroniser and use a plain 20MnCr5 dog-tooth range sleeve with 3° back-angle, shifting only when output speed is below 3 km/h with the 8-speed automatic in neutral. The transmission control unit pulses the gearbox input via the torque converter (or idles the gearbox in N) to bring sleeve slip speed below 30 rpm in <300 ms; the existing range actuator (12 V motor, ball-screw) then moves the sleeve. Toyota (Land Cruiser 250, GX 550) and the Ineos Grenadier (Tremec two-speed with manual lever) accept stopped or near-stopped range shifts, confirming customers in this class tolerate it. Luxury expectation is met by HMI: the driver presses LOW while rolling; the system completes the shift automatically as the car comes to rest.

title: Hinged front skid plate with two quarter-turn fasteners for oil and filter service
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] Fasteners −8 (cage nuts and bolts), drain access cover and its 3 fasteners deleted, plate gauge −25% via beads; dealer oil-service labour −0.2 h (warranty/service-plan cost). Baseline: front skid/sump guards on off-road MHEV SUVs are a single plate held by 8-12 M8/M10 bolts into cage nuts; each oil service requires removing and re-torquing all of them, cage nuts spin or seize after salt exposure (repair cost under warranty), and the plate contains a separate drain access cover with its own 2-4 fasteners. Proposal: hinge the front skid at its front edge on two cast-in pintle hooks engaging slots in the crash-beam lower flange, and retain the rear edge with two 1/4-turn captive steel fasteners (Rm ≥ 800 MPa, 12 kN shear rated) into PA66-GF50 receptacles plus two M10 bolts used only for heavy-duty off-road locking. A 3 mm EN AW-5083-H111 plate press-braked with two bead stiffeners replaces 4 mm plain plate (stiffness kept by beads). Service drops the rear edge; no drain hatch needed. Off-road benchmarks such as the GMC Hummer EV bolt on several separate skid plates and shields; our change is the attachment and service concept of the plate, not its material.

title: Replaceable PP lower apron raises approach angle without separate off-road bumper
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] One large painted fascia tool instead of two (two smaller apron tools ~€0.35M each added); paint variants halved; collision/off-road damage repair cost drops because the apron, not the painted fascia, takes the strike. Baseline: luxury SUVs that want both a road-car front end and a credible off-road approach angle often tool a separate "off-road" front bumper (different fascia moulding, chin and lamp apertures) — two large injection tools (~€1.5-€2.0M each) and paint variants. Defender 130 shows the geometric stakes: approach 37.5°, but departure drops to 28.5° vs 40° on the 90/110 because of overhang. Proposal: one painted fascia for all trims with a separate unpainted lower apron (PP-EPDM-T15, 3.0 mm, grained, mould-in-colour) clipped along a horizontal split line ~420 mm above ground. Road trim carries a deep apron with aero strakes; off-road trim carries a shallow apron that raises approach angle by ~3-4° (approx. 60 mm higher lower edge at 900 mm overhang). The apron is the sacrificial part: when it strikes rock it is replaced (€35-€50 part, 15 min) instead of a painted fascia (€450+ part plus paint). Same split applied at the rear for departure.

title: Ribbed thick-wall skid face moulded into MHEV tank; separate tank guard deleted
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] Deletes the separate tank guard, its brackets and fasteners; additional HDPE resin (~0.8-1.1 kg) and cradle redesign are cheaper than the guard. Saves ~3-5 kg. Baseline: MHEV off-road SUVs bolt a separate guard under the fuel tank — 2.5-3 mm steel or aluminium plate, or a PP-LGF30 moulding, with 4-6 brackets and 8-10 fasteners — because the normal 5-6 mm blow-moulded wall is not designed for sliding rock contact. Off-road benchmarks use many separate plates (GMC Hummer EV: five skid plates/rock sliders plus two shields). Proposal: make the tank its own skid. Program the parison wall (PWDS, 100-point profile) to 8-9 mm over the exposed lower footprint only, and mould a 6 mm-deep longitudinal rib pattern (ribs 5 mm wide, 35 mm pitch, 20° lead-in at the front edge) as a sliding face. The outer layer uses an abrasion-resistant UHMW-PE-modified polyethylene. Steel strap bands become two pressed 1.5 mm HX340LAD+Z cradles that carry the sliding load into the rails. Physics: the ribs share contact across several lands, and an 8-9 mm polyethylene section deforms elastically under a 0.6-0.8 kJ strike at −30 °C rather than cracking; a sacrificial clip-on wear strip covers the front 150 mm where most contact starts.

title: Long-stroke tripod plunge half-shaft instead of ball-spline shaft for off-road articulation
description: [800V BEV] [Off-road] Replaces the ball-spline section (precision ground tracks, balls, cage, seals) with a longer forged tripod housing; one extra machining length rather than a precision ball-spline assembly. Baseline: BEV off-roaders with large suspension travel need half-shafts that plunge far without binding. The GMC Hummer EV Heavy-Duty Off-Road Package fits ball-spline half-shafts specifically to improve articulation — a ball-spline intermediate section (hardened inner/outer races, 3-6 ball tracks, cage) plus a fixed CV at each end. Proposal: for our air-sprung BEV (front/rear travel ~250 mm with off-road height), use a conventional inboard tripod joint with an extended housing (plunge ±55 mm vs ±40 mm standard) and a 52 mm-stroke roller on needle bearings, shaft 41Cr4 induction-hardened tube Ø 34 × 6 mm, outboard Rzeppa fixed joint at 47° max angle. Geometry check: at full droop/off-road height the plunge requirement is ~42-48 mm and joint angle ~22° — inside tripod capability; the ball-spline is only needed for >60 mm plunge at high torque, typical of solid-axle-like travel. Peak wheel torque on BEV rear (~4.5 kNm) sits within a size-up of the standard tripod family.

title: Recovery eye forged in micro-alloyed 38MnVS6 with controlled cooling, no quench-temper
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes the quench-and-temper furnace step, straightening and associated energy (~0.4 kWh/kg) and logistics; 38MnVS6 bar is priced similar to or slightly below 42CrMo4. Baseline: screw-in or bolt-on recovery eyes on luxury SUVs are typically 42CrMo4 hot-forged, then quenched and tempered (Q&T to Rm 1,000-1,100 MPa), shot-blasted and zinc-flake coated; Q&T is an extra furnace route with straightening and hardness checks. Proposal: forge the eye in 38MnVS6 micro-alloyed steel and use controlled air cooling on a conveyor from the forging heat (BY route: ~1 °C/s through 800-500 °C), giving Rm 850-1,000 MPa, Rp0.2 ≥ 550 MPa and A ≥ 12% without Q&T. Size the eye shank (M24 → M27 or 2 mm larger section) to keep the rated load: a vehicle recovery eye on a 2.9 t SUV is typically proof-tested to ~2× GVW-related static pull; rated working load e.g. 4.5 t with safety factor 2 → 90 kN proof. Ineos documents rated front/rear recovery eyes spaced ~800/1,110 mm on the Grenadier for equaliser use; we keep a front pair and rear pair at platform-common thread.

title: Rear differential cover in ribbed EN-GJS-500-7 doubles as bash guard
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] Deletes the guard plate, two brackets and 4-6 fasteners and its fitting operation; the cover casting cost rises modestly (sand casting in iron vs HPDC aluminium) but net is positive. Baseline: MHEV off-road SUVs with an aluminium rear differential carrier and a pressed-steel or aluminium cover add a separate rear-diff guard (3-4 mm steel or aluminium plate with 4 brackets and 4-6 fasteners) because the cover cannot take rock contact. Proposal: cast the differential rear cover in EN-GJS-500-7 nodular iron, 5 mm nominal wall with a 12 mm-deep cross-ribbed lower face (ribs 6 mm thick at 40 mm pitch, 15° lead-in) that acts as the skid surface, and delete the separate guard. Mass of an iron cover (~3.6-4.2 kg) vs aluminium cover (~1.4 kg) + steel guard + brackets (~2.6-3.0 kg) is roughly neutral. Ribs also add ~20% oil-side surface for heat rejection in low-range crawl. The ductile iron absorbs a 2 kJ rock strike with local deformation rather than cracking (A ≥ 7%). The Hummer EV and Bronco Raptor show the market fits separate diff skid plates; we fold the function into the cover.

title: Road and all-terrain tyres in one size so off-road pack reuses the road wheel
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Deletes a wheel design and tool set (~€0.4-€0.6M), its finishing variant, a TPMS calibration set and a spare-wheel variant; aggregates wheel volume for piece-price leverage. Baseline: luxury SUVs offering an all-terrain pack usually add a dedicated wheel (smaller diameter, e.g. 20" vs road 22") so that a higher-sidewall AT tyre fits the wheel arch — a separate wheel design, forging/cast tool, finish variant, TPMS calibration and spare. Rivian bundles 20-inch All-Terrain wheels with the reinforced underbody shield and a full-size spare in its All-Terrain Upgrade. Proposal: freeze the tyre outer diameter at ~800 mm and specify both road and all-terrain tyres as 275/50 R21 (road: Grand-Touring compound, 8.5 mm tread; AT: 3PMSF-marked all-terrain, 11.5 mm tread, 3-ply sidewall) on one 21 × 9.5J flow-formed EN AC-42100 (AlSi7Mg0.3) wheel. Same OD keeps speedometer, ride-height calibration, wheel-arch clearance and brake package; AT sidewall at 50 series gives 137 mm, enough for airing down to 1.6 bar with a bead-retention hump. Only the tyre is a variant; wheel, TPMS and spare are common.

title: Front half-shaft bar in induction-hardened Cf53 replaces through-hardened 42CrMo4
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Cf53 bar is ~15-20% cheaper per kg than 42CrMo4; batch Q&T furnace route and straightening are replaced by an in-line scan-hardening cell; machining is easier on the softer bar before hardening. Baseline: off-road SUVs with lockers size front half-shaft bars for locked-axle peak torque (all torque through one wheel when the other is airborne), typically using 42CrMo4 quenched and tempered through the section (Rm 1,000-1,200 MPa), turned, splines rolled, then sometimes induction-hardened at the splines. Proposal: Cf53 (C53 for induction hardening) bar, cold-drawn, splines rolled, then scan induction-hardened over the full length to a case depth of 4-5 mm (~25-30% of a Ø30-32 mm bar radius) with a tempered martensite case (~55 HRC) and ferrite-pearlite core. Torsion stress peaks at the surface (τ = 16T/πd³), so a hard case carries the load: for 4.5 kNm peak on a Ø32 mm bar τmax ≈ 700 MPa, below the ~1,000 MPa torsional yield of the induction-hardened case; the softer core adds toughness against rock-impact bending. This is the standard route on many passenger-car half-shafts; we apply it to the off-road-rated shaft and size it to locked-axle torque (LC250 and GX 550 use rear lockers, Grenadier offers front and rear lockers, so peak single-wheel torque is the design case).

title: Hitch receiver cross-member roll-formed from S420MC replaces welded tube assembly
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Material mass −15-20% through higher yield, weld length −70%, part count from ~11 to 3; roll-forming is cheaper per metre than tube cutting and bracket welding. Baseline: OEM tow bars for 3,500 kg SUVs (Defender 110: 3,500 kg, 150 kg nose weight) use a welded cross-member of S355J2 hollow section (80 × 60 × 4 mm) with four welded brackets, gussets and a receiver socket — 9-12 parts, ~2.2 m of MAG weld, then e-coat. Proposal: a single closed-section cross-member roll-formed and laser-welded from 3.0 mm S420MC (Rp0.2 ≥ 420 MPa), variable section (hat with closing plate, 90 × 70 mm at centre tapering to 70 × 60 mm at the rail ends), with the rail-mounting flanges formed in-line and pierced on the roll-form line. Section modulus at the receiver: 4 mm S355 tube W ≈ 38 cm³ vs 3 mm S420MC 90 × 70 hat W ≈ 36 cm³ — bending capacity W × Rp equals ~15.1 vs ~13.5 kN·m, so S420MC at 3 mm with the larger section meets the D-value (≈18 kN) load case with the same margin as the baseline. Brackets reduce to two pressed end-plates; weld length to ~0.6 m. Common across MHEV (3,500 kg) and BEV (lower rating) — BEV uses the same part.

title: Wheel-speed sensor lead rides the brake hose in one TPV guide, corner bracket deleted
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Per corner it deletes the separate stamped WSS bracket, 2-3 steel P-clips and one EPDM grommet, plus the extra bolt and its torque operation. The added part is one small injection-moulded guide. The single shared routing loop also removes one articulation validation per corner variant (standard and off-road height) from the test plan. Baseline: a long-travel off-road corner (about 500 mm of cross-axle articulation and roughly 145 mm of extra lift on air suspension, as on the Defender L663) needs extra free length in the flexible brake hose and the wheel-speed sensor (WSS) lead. Most corners route the two separately: the brake hose runs from a body bracket to a stamped DC04 intermediate bracket on the knuckle or strut, and the WSS lead follows its own path with a second stamped bracket on the upper control arm, 2-3 steel P-clips and an EPDM grommet. Each loop is validated on its own, and each is a chafe risk when the wheel is at full droop or full bump. Proposal: route the WSS lead along the brake hose in one injection-moulded twin-channel guide. A PA66-GF30 clip snaps onto the hose crimp ferrules at each end, with a TPV (Shore 80A) overmoulded channel that holds the lead at 3-4 points along the hose. The hose then sets the bend radius for both, so the lead cannot be pinched outside the hose envelope, and one shared intermediate bracket replaces two.

Each loop is validated on its own, and each is a chafe risk when the wheel is at full droop or full bump. Proposal: route the WSS lead along the brake hose in one injection-moulded twin-channel guide. A PA66-GF30 clip snaps onto the hose crimp ferrules at each end, with a TPV (Shore 80A) overmoulded channel that holds the lead at 3-4 points along the hose. The hose then sets the bend radius for both, so the lead cannot be pinched outside the hose envelope, and one shared intermediate bracket replaces two. The WSS lead length is matched to the hose (one tolerance stack instead of two), and the lead is specified as a high-flex cable class (fine-strand conductor, TPE jacket) because it now follows the hose motion exactly.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Corner assembly loses one bracket bolt-down and the P-clip fitting: about 20-25 s per corner, or about 80-100 s per vehicle. The guide clips on at the hose supplier (pre-assembled hose and lead kit), so the vehicle line installs one kit per corner. New tooling is one 4-cavity injection tool with overmould, about €60-80k. The stamped bracket die is retired.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Part count drops by 4-5 per corner (bracket, bolt, 2-3 P-clips, grommet), about 16-20 per vehicle. The guide is keyed to the hose ferrule flats, so it cannot be fitted rotated. One kit replaces two separately routed items, which removes the common error of crossing the WSS lead over the hose at full lock. Service is simpler: a replacement hose comes with its guide.

costSavingPotential.percentage: 15-25% of the corner brake-hose and WSS routing hardware cost
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Per corner: bracket €0.55-€0.70 + 2-3 P-clips €0.20-€0.30 + grommet and bolt €0.15-€0.20 + 20-25 s assembly at €50/h €0.28-€0.35 = €1.18-€1.55; minus the new guide €0.45-€0.50 (including tool amortisation of €70k over 7 years × 200,000 corners/yr) = €0.60-€0.90 net per corner. × 4 corners = €2.4-€3.6 per vehicle × 50,000 vehicles/yr = €0.12M-€0.18M/yr. Estimate; excludes any warranty reduction from fewer chafe failures.

Validate: articulation flex test of the hose and lead kit at full droop, full bump and full lock (for example 1 million cycles with temperature cycling); brake hose requirements to FMVSS 106 / ISO 3996 with the guide fitted; WSS signal integrity under vibration to ISO 16750-3; mud and stone ingress on an off-road durability route. Mitigation: a high-flex lead specification and a sacrificial wear rib in the channel.

title: Transfer-case range fork in PA46-GF30 with overmoulded steel pads
description: [MHEV] [Off-road] Removes casting + machining (bore, pad faces) + pad assembly; one moulding (35-40 s cycle, 2-cavity) with insert loading. Lower mass reduces actuator force spec slightly. Baseline: the high/low range fork in a two-speed transfer case (as on Defender, Land Cruiser 250, Grenadier) is typically a nodular-iron or aluminium die-cast fork, machined at the rail bore and pad faces, with bronze or nylon pad inserts — or a forged steel fork. Proposal: injection-mould the fork body in PA46-GF30 (HDT ~290 °C @1.8 MPa, retains ~60% stiffness at 150 °C in ATF), overmoulding two 16MnCr5 case-hardened sliding pads and a steel rail bushing so no machining is needed. Fork force on a dog-type range sleeve (≤ 900 N with a motor/ball-screw actuator at standstill shift — see synchroniser-delete idea) gives a bending stress of ~35-45 MPa in a 10 × 18 mm ribbed section, below PA46-GF30 long-term strength at 150 °C conditioned (~70-80 MPa). Mass falls from ~0.55 kg (iron) to ~0.18 kg. PA46 is the standard choice for polymer shift forks in manual transmissions; here it is applied to a low-duty, few-shifts-per-life range fork.

Fork force on a dog-type range sleeve (≤ 900 N with a motor/ball-screw actuator at standstill shift — see synchroniser-delete idea) gives a bending stress of ~35-45 MPa in a 10 × 18 mm ribbed section, below PA46-GF30 long-term strength at 150 °C conditioned (~70-80 MPa). Mass falls from ~0.55 kg (iron) to ~0.18 kg. PA46 is the standard choice for polymer shift forks in manual transmissions; here it is applied to a low-duty, few-shifts-per-life range fork.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Removes casting + machining (bore, pad faces) + pad assembly; one moulding (35-40 s cycle, 2-cavity) with insert loading. Lower mass reduces actuator force spec slightly.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Moulder with an insert-loading robot; tool ~€70k (2-cavity). Removes the machining fixture and two machining operations (~70 s) and the separate pad assembly; casting porosity scrap is eliminated.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Part count −2 (pads integrated); pad position fixed by the mould, so there is no fork-to-pad tolerance stack; an asymmetric rail bush prevents reverse fitting on the shift rail.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Low — small part on every MHEV transfer case
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Per MHEV transfer case: casting + machining + pad assembly €6.5-€8.0 vs moulded fork with inserts €3.5-€4.0 = €3.0-€4.0 saving × MHEV share 50-55% of 50,000 → €1.5-€2.2 per vehicle (fleet average). Range €1.5-€2.2 per vehicle (fleet average) × 50,000 vehicles/yr = €0.07M-€0.11M/yr.

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: creep and ATF ageing of PA46 at 150 °C; impact during clash. Validate: 3,000 h ATF immersion at 150 °C with property retention, 20,000 shift-cycle endurance at −30/+120 °C, ISO 16750-3 vibration, fork-tip deflection under 1,500 N misuse.

title: Locker engagement sensed from actuator current signature; delete Hall position sensor
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Removes the sensor, magnet, sealed connector, harness branch and axle-housing machining for the sensor port; replaces with software in the existing actuator driver. Baseline: electronic differential lockers (Defender Active Locking Rear Differential, Grenadier optional e-lockers, Land Cruiser 250 rear e-locker) confirm dog engagement with a dedicated sensor — a Hall or reed switch with magnet on the dog ring, sealed connector, 3-wire harness through the axle housing. That sensor and its connector are a known water-ingress and fault-code source in wading duty. Proposal: delete the sensor and infer engagement from the electromagnetic actuator's own electrical signature: when the dog ring closes the magnetic air gap, coil inductance rises ~30-40%, so the current rise time under PWM changes measurably; the driver IC (smart high-side with current sense, already in the zone controller) measures di/dt each PWM period. Cross-check with wheel-speed sensors: a locked axle forces left/right wheel speeds equal within 0.5% while turning on low-µ. Combined, engagement is confirmed within 150-250 ms. Applies to the common MHEV/BEV rear locker cartridge.

title: Aluminium magnet-wire coil in e-locker solenoid replaces copper winding
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Copper (~€9-€10/kg) replaced by aluminium magnet wire (~€4-€5/kg as wire); conductor mass halves despite the larger section, so conductor cost falls ~65-70%. Housing grows slightly (small added steel). Baseline: electromagnetic differential lockers (Defender Active Locking Rear Differential, Land Cruiser 250 / GX 550 rear e-lockers, Grenadier optional front/rear lockers) are actuated by an axial solenoid coil wound with enamelled copper magnet wire (grade 2, class 200 °C polyamide-imide), typically 0.25-0.35 kg of copper per coil, potted in an oil-immersed steel pole housing. Proposal: wind the coil with enamelled aluminium magnet wire (EC-grade Al 99.5, class 200 °C overcoat). Aluminium has ~61% of copper's conductivity, so for the same ampere-turns and resistance the conductor cross-section rises ~1.6× and the winding window ~1.3-1.4× with the same fill factor; the pole housing gains ~3 mm axial length. Duty is benign: the locker is engaged at most a few hundred times a year with a 12 V, ~3 A hold current after a 1 s pull-in pulse — winding temperature rise in 90-120 °C oil is <20 K. Mass of conductor falls ~50% (Al density 2.70 vs Cu 8.96 g/cm³). Terminations use ultrasonic welding to copper-clad tabs, a proven route on aluminium-wound motors and solenoids.

title: Fine-blanked 16MnCr5 locker dog ring replaces machined forging
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] [Off-road] Replaces forge + turn + mill dogs + broach (4 ops) with one press stroke at ~30-40 strokes/min; material utilisation improves, machining time drops ~80%; LPC gas quench removes press-quench and straightening. Baseline: the sliding dog ring in electronic differential lockers is usually a hot-forged ring blank of 20MnCr5 or 18CrNiMo7-6, turned, then the face dogs are milled or shaped (12-18 dogs), splines broached, case-carburised and ground — 5-6 operations. Proposal: fine-blank the dog ring from 8 mm 16MnCr5 strip (annealed, spheroidised) on a 6,300 kN triple-action press, forming the face dogs as a semi-pierced/coined profile and the internal spline in the same stroke (fine-blanking sheared-edge share >90%), then low-pressure carburise (0.6-0.8 mm CHD) with gas quench to keep distortion <30 µm, and only finish-grind the spline OD datum. Dog loading check: rear axle peak locked torque ~15 kNm (MHEV low range) shared by 16 dogs at 42 mm mean radius gives ~22 kN per dog; with 8 mm dog height and 6 mm engagement contact stress stays within carburised 16MnCr5 limits (~1,500 MPa surface). Fine-blanking is widely used for clutch hubs and parking-lock pawls; applied here to the locker cartridge shared by MHEV and BEV (Defender, Grenadier and Land Cruiser use electronic lockers that rely on such a dog clutch).

title: 925 V-class pack keeps 400 kW charging under 500 A, shrinking contactors and busbars
description: [800V BEV] Charging current, not voltage, sizes the expensive copper and switching hardware. Cutting peak current ~20% downgrades contactors and pyro-fuse one rating class, removes ~20% of main busbar copper and deletes liquid cooling on the pack-side charge leads; extra AFE channels for ~20 more series cells are the only adder. Baseline: a ~105 kWh luxury-SUV pack configured around 800 V nominal (roughly 190-200 NMC cells in series, ~620-830 V window). To advertise 400 kW peak DC charging the pack must accept ~610-650 A at the low-SOC voltage (~650 V), which forces 630 A-class main and DC-charge contactors, ~120 mm² copper main busbars, a liquid-cooled pack-side charge harness and 630 A pyro-fuse. Proposal: re-string the same chemistry to ~216-220 series cells (max ~925 V, ~780 V at 10% SOC) at unchanged energy by using a ~10% smaller-capacity cell or 1p instead of 2p groups. At 780 V, 400 kW needs only ~513 A, so the pack moves to 500 A-class contactors and pyro-fuse, main busbars drop to ~95 mm² Cu (I²R held constant at equal temperature rise), and the pack-side DC charge leads stay passively cooled. Inverters already use 1200 V SiC MOSFETs at 800 V, so semiconductor rating is unchanged; only insulation coordination moves to the 1000 V DC class (IEC 60664-1 creepage ≈ +15%). Benchmarks: NIO ES8 (2025) runs a 900 V platform with 925 V maximum; Lucid Gravity runs 926 V for 400
