title: MHEV tunnel shield: aluminised needle-punched PET felt replaces foil-plus-felt laminate
description: [MHEV] Material: foil + shoddy laminate (€9-11) → aluminised PET felt (€6-7.5); EVA patch area −40% (€1.5-2); bonding step removed (€1). ~0.4 kg lighter. Net €4-6 per MHEV. Baseline: the MHEV cabin-side tunnel insulator over the 8-speed automatic and exhaust is typically a laminate of 0.1 mm embossed aluminium foil bonded to a resinated cotton-shoddy or glass-fibre felt (1,400-1,800 g/m²), plus a separate EVA heavy layer patch over the gearbox bell-housing — 3 materials, 2 bonding steps, ~2.4 kg. Proposal: replace with a single needle-punched PET felt (1,600 g/m², bicomponent PET binder fibre, thermoformed at 190 °C for 45 s) with a vacuum-metallised aluminised PET film facing (12 µm) laminated in-line on the felt line; reflectivity >85% in IR. The EVA patch is reduced to the zone above the bell-housing only. BEV derivative does not need the part at all (flat floor, no exhaust) so the cost sits only on MHEV. Benchmark: JLR quantifies a 7 dB NVH reduction for the Range Rover Electric vs the V8 model, confirming that tunnel/exhaust-related insulation is MHEV-specific content worth optimising separately rather than commonising into the BEV.

title: Seat side-airbag tear seam in trim cover replaces plastic deployment housing
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Deleted per seat: hard housing €2.5-3.5 and clips €0.4; added chute strap €0.8-1.0. Net €2-3 per seat; 2 front seats (+2 rear on 40% with rear side bags) → €4.5-7.5 per vehicle, quoted €4-7. Baseline: seat-integrated thorax/pelvis side airbags are commonly packed in an injection-moulded PA6-GF30 or TPO hard housing (~120-160 g) bolted to the seat-back side member, with a separate fabric "chute" or guide sleeve sewn into the cover so the bag exits through the seam — housing + chute + clips. Proposal: soft-pack the side airbag in a PA66 fabric wrap with 2 integrated mounting studs, and use a force-directing chute made of a non-stretch PA66 woven strap (60-80 mm wide) sewn into the cover seam (tear seam of reduced-tenacity thread, defined stitch length 4 mm) and anchored to the seat frame, so the frame and the strap guide the bag; the hard housing is deleted. Benchmark: Volvo’s EX90 support literature describes thorax side bags integrated in the front seat backrests, and Kia lists dual front seat-mounted side bags on the EV9 — in both, the cover seam rather than a visible door defines the bag exit, which is what makes a housing-free soft-pack feasible.

title: Thixomoulded semi-solid AZ91D cockpit beam, 2.0 mm walls, replaces welded steel tube
description: [MHEV & 800V BEV] Steel beam (tube + 25 brackets + welding ~€58-68) vs semi-solid Mg (4.8 kg × Mg alloy ~€3.2-3.6/kg + process ~€35-40) ≈ €52-58: ~€4-10 cheaper at today’s Mg/Al price ratio; plus fewer GA bolts (steering column bracket integrated) €2-3 and BIW mass benefit. Sensitive to Mg price. Baseline: many luxury SUVs use a welded steel cross-car beam — a Ø50-60 mm HSLA tube (S420MC, 1.8-2.0 mm) with 20-30 stamped brackets (steering column, HVAC, IP, glovebox, A-pillar feet, tunnel braces) MAG-welded on a robotic line — ~9-11 kg. Conventional HPDC magnesium beams cut mass but need 2.5-3.0 mm walls for fill and have porosity that limits ductility. Proposal: a semi-solid (thixomoulded) AZ91D beam: Mg chips heated to ~590 °C semi-solid state (30-40% solid fraction) and injected at lower temperature and turbulence than HPDC, allowing 2.0 mm nominal walls with lower porosity; all 20-30 brackets integrated in one casting; steel inserts only at the steering-column mounting for stiffness; 0.8 mm e-coat + isolating washers against galvanic corrosion to steel A-pillar. Target mass 4.5-5.0 kg; part count 25 → 3. Benchmark: the first semi-solid Mg IP crossbeam has entered series production for Seres’ AITO models, weighing less than half of a traditional steel counterpart at a stable 1,000 units/day; GF Casting Solutions’ Mg cross-car beam for the Mercedes S-Class won the European Die

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Removes robotic MAG weld line (~€6M) and 25 bracket dies at supplier; thixomoulding cell (≈1,600 t) cycle ~60-75 s. CNC machining of 6 datum faces (40 s). Scrap lower than HPDC (less porosity rejection).

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Medium — cost-neutral to positive with major weight saving (≈5 kg)

ideaData.riskNotes: Risks: galvanic corrosion to steel body (isolate per VDA 233-102 cyclic test), steering-column vibration (first mode ≥ 38-40 Hz target), crash behaviour (IIHS small overlap intrusion, FMVSS 208), creep at elevated temperature (AZ91D limited above 120 °C — keep away from HVAC heater outlets), Mg price volatility. How this differs: We specify the semi-solid route specifically to reach 2.0 mm walls and full bracket integration on a luxury SUV beam, replacing a welded steel beam rather than HPDC Mg.
